Subject: Judicious use of Modes of Correspondence
Sir,
4714 2011
It has been noticed that the modes of correspondence available in the
offices of the Organisation are not often used scrupulously, e.g., while a letter is
sent through speed post, it is faxed also; or, a circular which is posted on the
website of the Organisation also follows the same conduit. This practice results
in loss of time, energy and other scarce resources of the Organisation.
In the light of the above, the following instructions as regard to
correspondence between the offices are listed below for strict compliance with
immediate effect.
A.
Instructions for Head Office:
a)
All the Communications which have common concern to all field
offices, like Circulars, Reports, intimations etc., will be displayed by the
Head Office on the website of the Organisation. This display shall not be
followed by any written communications like fax, speed or general post.
b)
The material displayed at website will be considered as 'Circulated'
hence no hard copy will be circulated among sections and officers in Head
Office. The issuing officer may, however, exercise his discretion
cautiously for any exception.
c)
The other communications which are specific to certain office will
be sent through e-mail on the official e-mail ID of that office. The NIC has
already provided an e-mail ID to all the offices of the EPFO which is
placed at (Annexure-'A').
d)
The officers upto the rank of RPFC-II have also been provided with
an individual e-mail ID (Annexure-'B') in the epfindia.gov.in domain. This
may be used by them while communicating to each other in individual
capacity for facilitating officework.
1

B.
Instructions for Field Offices:
a)
The. Field Offices shall use official e-mails for all sorts of information
to all offices including higher offices and their subordinate offices.
C.
General Instructions:
i)
Each and every officer will check his/her mailbox and official
website of the Organisation as . routine function. The related
information may be downloaded/printed as per requirement only.
ii)
It may be mentioned that while information flowing between two
Individual IDs may not require a signature, the communications
passing through official e-mail IDs may require one. In such cases,
the scanned copy of the correspondence may be sent as
attachments.
iii)
The serial number of communication on the webpage is to be used
for further reference so that hard copies are not required all the
time to refer this piece of communication. This will also save time
in searching out the references.
All confidential communications requiring physical delivery shall,
however, be sent by post as usual and will not be subject to the
instructions contained in this circular.
It is further intimated that no excuses will be entertained in
implementation of the above order. Any violation of the same will be viewed
seriously. The suggestions, if any, for improvement may be forwarded to FA &
CAO. The queries regarding e-mail IDs/passwords etc. may, however, be
addressed to RPFC (NDC).
(This issues with the approval of CPFC)

Sub: Revised Instructions for allotment of code no under section 1(3)(a) & 1(3)(b) of
EPF & MP Act, 1952 and securing compliance - regarding

Sir,

The allotment of ‘Code No. is an aiminidtniive process for registration and
identification of ‘an establishment’ covered under ithe Act alongwith maintenance of
accounts of members vis-d-vis remittances made so as to extend social security benefits
to them,

While on one hand it is to be ensured that all the eligible employees of an
establishment get due benefits under the provisions of Act and schemes framed thereunder, on the other, we have to.ascertain that such provisions are not misused and Code
No(s) are not issued in haste to ineligible cases. The existing practice of issuance of code
no within three days has already created concerns which have been attempted to be
addressed by the Finance Wing’s circular no WSU/17(2)2000/Clarification/103414 dated
11.03.2011.

The field offices have pointed out that the three days time period allowed for
allotment of code number is too short to verify the genuineness and authenticity of
documents and information submitted by an establishment while submitting the
application for code number. The feedbacks received from the field offices are therefore
considered and the following revised guidelines are issued in supersession of earlier
guidelines/directions on the related i issue:

1. The processing time for’ ainiuent of code number shall be thirty days from
the date of the receipt of coverage proposal in the office including the time
taken by Enforcement Officers for verification of details of the Coverage
Application Form.

2. No Code No. shall be allotted without conducting inspection by the field
machinery to verify the existence of establishment and genuineness of the
details provided by the employer in the coverage application form. The
documents in support of date of set up, nature of activity, address, bank
details, PAN/TAN; etc in respect of establishment as well as address and other
details of Employer(s) should also be invariably be scrutinized and verified as
per existing instructions.

Contd...

3. The requirement of advance deposit of one month contributions is not as per
the provisions of the Act and Schemes and as such the system of collecting a
Demand Draft for such advance contributions shall be discontinued for the
purpose of allotment of Code No.

4. There would be no change to the existing coverage proforma as circulated
vide circular no. Compliance 2001/Circular/E-1/44946 dated 31.08.2000.

5. Non-adherence to the time limit prescribed as above shal] be viewed seriously.

6. While implementing the revised instructions, RPFCs/OICs shall ensure that all
the coverable establishments should be covered and the benefits are extended
to all eligible euployyer:

The above guidelines shall. come into force with immediate effect. Please
acknowledge the receipt. .

(This issues with the approval of the CPFC)

(K.C, Pandey)
- Addl. Central P. F. Commissioner (Compliance)

Sub: Inoperative Accounts - Modalities for payment out of Inoperative
Accounts.

Sir,

In the 190" meeting of CBT, EPF held on 15.09.2010, it was decided that no
interest shall be credited to the account of a member from the first day of its
becoming inoperative i.e. from 37" month. This is to be effective from 01.04.2011.
Copy of Gazette Notification issued by the Ministry of Labour & Employment, Govt.
of India has already bzen circulated by Head Office letter No.
Coord/3(2)2010/inoperative Accounts/92370 dated 25.01.2011 to all the field offices
of EPFO at Sl. Nd. 465 of the official website.

pz For finalising the modalities and to ensure correct identification and
genuineness of the beneficiary alongwith correctness of the amount for
settlement/authorisation of claims out of Inoperative Accounts, an agenda item was
placed before the CBT, EPF in its 192nd meeting held on 15.02.2011 wherein
following modalities/ procedures have been approved: -

a) In all such cases where the establishment is functioning and employer is
available, the attestation of claim forms by the authorized signatory should
be mandatory

b) In those cases where employer is not available to identify the member, the
attestation by the Bank authorities should be insisted alongwith at least
one of the documents as required under KYC (Know Your Customer)
towards identity proof (ID) and proof of residence. These are:

i. PAN Card
ii. Voters Identity Card
iii. Passport
iv. Ration Card
v. ESI Identity Card
vi. Copy of electricity/water/landline telephone bill in the name of
the claimant with the present address.
vii. Driving license, if applicable
viii. Any other identity card issued by the Government authority.

c) A multilevel verifications/counter checking should be done to ensure
correct identification and genuineness of the beneficiary alongwith
correctness of the amount. Taking this into account, following delegation
of power to authorize/settle claims out of Inoperative accounts has been
made: -

i) Account Officer (AO) in charge of Accounts Groups may authorize
claims upto Rs. 50,000/- out of Inoperative Accounts provided
the same is counter checked by another AQ.

ii) APFC may authorize claims for Rs. 50,000/- and above out of
Inoperative accounts provided the same is counter checked by
another APFC or in absence of an APFC by an AO.

The above instructions shall be followed scrupulously while settling the cases
out of inoperative accounts. All care shall be taken to reduce the risk of frauds and
to ensure that the claims are authentic and the payments are made to the genuine
claimants.

Yours faithfully,

Ae

(Rajesn Bansal)

Subject:
National Workshop for Representatives of Exempted Establishments on
24-25 March 2011 – Inviting of Nominations - Regarding.

Sir,

The National Academy for Training & Research in Social Security has been conducting National
Workshops for the Exempted Establishment under Employees’ Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act,
1952 for the last several years. Your involvement in collecting the nominations from the establishments has been
very supportive in making the programme a success. Many participants felt that there should be more such
programmes every year as the contents of the programme were really educative for them to accomplish the tasks
before them in administering the fund.

As per the requests of the participants in the earlier programs, and keeping in view the developments in
EPF and EPS Administration, we have designed a two day National Workshop on 24th and 25th March 2011.

In the Workshop, we propose to cover all relevant issues like:


Discussing the provisions of the Act and the Schemes

Identify the issues involved in compliance management of exemption

State the nature and periodicity of returns from exempted establishments

Sorting out processes and procedures for better coordination and cooperation

Discuss the investment pattern for provident funds

A copy of programme announcement and a copy of the Nomination form are enclosed.

You are, therefore, requested to collect 4-6 nominations from your Region for this programme and send to
us.

Keeping in view the requirement of Exempted Establishments and their interest to participate in the programme, we
have kept the participation fee for Residential participants Rs.8,000/- per participants covering boarding and
lodging, course material etc. and Rs.6,000/- per participants for those not availing accommodation at
NATRSS will be given study material and day lunch. However, the stay arrangements have been made for
nominated person(s) in the campus of the Academy by the evening of previous day i.e. 23.03.2011 and next day
morning of the programme.

The Demand Draft drawn in favour of National Academy for Training & Research in Social Security
payable at New Delhi towards participation fee paid by the establishment concerned shall be sent to the Academy
preferably before 16th March, 2011. For any further clarification or query you may contact the undersigned at
Phone No.011-28521199, or e-mail: natrss@hotmail.com.
(This issues with the approval of the Director, NATRSS).
Yours faithfully,

Sub: Advise to use e-mail services of NIC.IN or ERNET from security point of viewregarding.
Sir,
This is to inform that as per the observation of the Ministry.of Home Affairs received
through the Ministry of Labour and Employment, it has been found that many senior officers
in the Government of India are using e-mail IDs having foreign domain names like YAHOO,
H.OTMAIL, G-Mail, AOL etc for official communication purpose • and since the internet
traffic of these e-mail providers are routed through and stored • on servers located abroad
making it easily accessible for the intelligence agencies of these countries. It has also been
observed that it is also possible to spoof the e-mail address
, and send e-mails which might
cause serious embarrassment to the owner of the e-mail ID .and if this happens in the case of
important Government functionaries, the damage could be serious.
In view of the above facts, Ministry of Home Affairs , has requested that officers in the
Government of India may strictly be instructed to use e-mail IDs like NIC.IN or ERNET from
security point of view. Only these e-mail IDs should be printed on their letter heads and used
for official communication through e-mail. Subordinate anti public sector offices under the
Ministries have also been advised to take necessary action on the above lines.
The above mentioned advice has been received from the Ministry of Labour and
Employment for following the instructions.
All officers of EPFO are thereby requested to adhere to the instructions and not use the
e-mail IDs having foreign domains for any official communication and also not to print such
IDs in letter heads.. Official e-mail IDs for all offices and by name to officers up to RPFC II
level have been allotted and communicated to them.
It is also to inform that any communication sent through the e-mail IDs allotted with
domain name "epfindia.gov.in " to the offices and officers may be treated as official
communication_

Dear Commissioner,

As you are aware, compliance is a critical function of EPFO, and its
importance can hardly be overemphasized. However, you will agree that
compliance scenario as it obtains today, is less than desirable and this function
including the functionaries engaged in this function at times has drawn adverse
criticism from various stakeholders of EPFO. Accordingly, a need has been felt to
strengthen the compliance function of EPFO by way of professionalization of the
compliance functionaries.

2. There are multitude of factors impinging upon the effectiveness of
compliance function viz., statutory, structural, systemic etc. However, one of
the main contributing factors in this regard is the inadequate
capacities of compliance functionaries in terms of their knowledge and skill
to effectively. discharge their functions. Training, retraining and certification are
time tested and cost effective tools to address the competency gaps and achieve
the goal of professionalization of staff. It is in this context that a proposal has
been drafted for competency development of APFCs in first stage.

3; It is proposed to administer a comprehensive test to take
stock of the existing level of knowledge & skill of APFCs in compliance
function. The test will be in the form of objective type format. Only those
officers who possess minimum stipulated standard of knowledge and skill as
demonstrated in the test will be posted in compliance function. Those who
fail to qualify the assessment test will be trained and developed through
specifically designed training modules in the NATRSS. The first assessment test
will be scheduled sometimes in March end 2011.

Sub: - Provision of air-conditioner at various offices building.

Sir,

The proposal on the above subject having the estimated value Rs. 36.00
Crores was placed before the 68" EC meeting held on 06/08/2010 in which the
matter has been discussed and decided that the proposal contained in the
memorandum was approved in principal by the EC subject to the condition that
it will be cleared by the finance division before finalizing the procurement.
Accordingly the proposal was submitted to finance wing for concurrence and
allocation of the budget but the finance wing raised the observation that fixing
up a monetary limit of Rs. 36 crores may not be appropriate and cost of the ACs,
including the installation cost requisite changes in ceilings etc. be worked out

with the consultation of the expert and only then be put up for financial
concurrence.

During the 69" EC meeting held on 08/12/2010 attention were focused on
the Action taken report on 68" EC minutes of meeting by the committee and
observed by the Chairman CBT that the decision of the EC on the above subject
agenda item was not recorded correctly and decided to be amended as below.

“ The chairman indicated that the provisioning of air conditioning facility was
important for EPFO offices It is important to modernize the offices not only for
providing good working conditions but to have better output. The member
visiting EPFO offices should also feel comfortable. He observed that the agenda
may be approved by the committee and RPFCs in-charge may be authorized to

install the air-conditioners in the offices to facilitate computerization after
following the GFR procedure laid down and the CVC guidelines.”

On the basis of directions of 69" EC, the proposal was processed to
finance wing for concurrence and allocation of the budget which has been

concurred. The following points may be considered while taking the steps for
execution of the air — conditioning work.

1. Officer in charge of concerned RO/SRO may call the reputed AC provider
for inspection of the building and to suggest for installation of the airconditioning unit suitable to the design of the constructed building. The
detail drawing to be prepared mentioning the existing used of the area
proposed for air conditioning. Unused area such as lift lobby, toilet,
bathroom etc of the building should not be included for air-conditioning
purpose.

. On the basis of the average area of various field offices, the following

bench mark is prescribed to calculate air-conditioning area and the
estimated cost their-of.

Type of office Tentative Tonnage Approximate
Appx. Area Estimated cost
Regional office (Metro) 2500Sq Mtr 200 TR Rs.37, 22,700/-
Regional office 1800Sq Mtr 150 TR Rs. 28, 23,600/-
SROs 1000Sq Mtr 90 TR Rs.18, 72,900/-

. The possibility will be explored to accommodate the split/window type
AC units of the reputed brand having minimum 03 star energy efficient
approved by BEE, in the offices.

. In any case, it is not possible to install the spilt/window type unit in the
existing building, the provision of packaged type AC may be opted.

. A comprehensive proposal may be prepared in two part firstly based on
the DGS&D rate and second on market rate, according to the report of AC
provider. The availability of the AC Units on DGS&D rate contract can
be seen/ verified on DGS&D website www.dgsnd.gov.in . Presently
window / split type AC units are available on DGS&D rate contract.
Regarding procurement & installation of the packaged type unit, the
proposal may be asked from Govt. /semi govt. agency.

Sub: Handling of Transfer cases in new software - Reg.
Sir
The Central Board of Trustees, EPF in its 191 st meeting held on 09-12-2010 had
considered and approved the revised procedure for settlement of transfer claims (Form
13) in respect of members who have changed employment from one un-exempted
establishment to another un-exempted establishment. Under the revised procedure
transfer of accounts in such instances shall be treated at par with the final settlement
cases. The procedure involves transfer of funds between offices (in the case of interregional transfer) through the NEFT mode alongwith electronic transfer and upload of
the Annexure 'K' file credit to the new member should be approved with the signed
copy of Annexure 'K'. The revised process is expected to speed up the process of
settlement of transfer cases. The details of the new process is attached herewith
(Annexure A).
The application software of the 'modernization project' has been modified
accordingly and has been tested at four offices namely (RO, Faridabad, Delhi (N),
Gurgaon & SRO, Karnal). Delhi (N) has also confirmed the pilot tested to be
successful. The Internal Finance Division has concurred the concept & necessary
changes in the Manual of Accounting Procedure (MAP) are being carried out which will
be communicated to all the offices in due course.
To
JAN
(177:7 7

The modified. software containing intra-alia the revised procedure mentioned
above is being released and all offices which have migrated to the new application shall
implement the same with immediate effect for both transfer-in & transfer-out cases.
However, the offices that are yet to implement the new application shall receive the
Annexure 'K' file and confirm receipt of funds in bank statement (through NEFT).
However credit to members' accounts in such offices will be given only in the new
system. Importantly, such offices will keep on hold transfer-out-cases till
implementation of the new system. The agenda item on the subject approved by CBT
and minutes. (extract) is also annexed for your information.
This new features is to be implemented with immediate effect in all the offices
as stated above.

11.11.1.
PROCEDURE FOR TRANSFER OF ACCOUNT OF A MEMBER IN
REGIONAL/SUB REGIONAL OFFICES WHERE NEW
APPLICATION SOFTWARE IS IMPLEMENTED:
The procedure for transfer of Account of a member mentioned in this
Chapter at Paras 11.1.1. to 11.10.2. will be followed with the
following modifications :
a) In case of transfers from one unexempted establishment to
another unexempted establishment either in the same office
or to the other office, interest for the broken currency period
will be calculated like final settlement.
b) In case of transfer from one office to another, the actual
transfer of funds will be effected through National Electronic
Fund Transfer (NEFT).
c) The transferee office on receipt of the Amended AnnexureK(Revised) [Copy of the Amended Annexure-K(Revised) is
provided at Para-11.11.2.
, will credit only the opening
balance of the last financial year plus contribution for the
broken currency period minus withdrawals, if any, as if
contribution received in the month upto which the transferring
office calculated interest.
d) The interest calculated by the transferring office will be
credited to the member's account in the last month of the
current financial year or in the month in which final settlement
of claim is made whichever is earlier.

Attention is drawn to the Audit Report of Internal Audit Parties handed to the respective
Officers-in-charge of the Sub-Regional and Regional Offices as part of annual audit
activity. All officers may be aware that Audit is a statutory requirement cast on all
government bodies for more responsible and responsive working. Responding to

audit observations in a time-bound manner , is of utmost importance and the OIC
concerned must personally focus his attention on the observations made by the IAP. The
obserrvations in IAR are useful tools in the hands of the OIC to monitor, control and
improve the efficiency of the office and are therefore to be welcomed.
ft is found that most of the offices do not take audit observations seriously and do not
send compliance to the audit observations, more so in a time bound manner. Even while
sending the replies many offices send the replies through a lower level officer instead of
under the signature of the OIC. It may be noted that the OIC is responsible for funishing
replies to the Audit and therefore all replies must be invariably sent under the signature of
the OIC only Any reply, received under the signature of any other officer would be
treated as not received and returned to the originating office.
Further many offices send Interim Replies in the form of `being looked into', 'being
processed. / done', 'a letter has been issued to ...', 'will .be done', etc. These replies do
not serve any purpose and such replieS need not be sent as this would only be waste,of
time, energy and money for the Organisation.
For the Observations to be dropped, full compliance must be reported by completing the
desirable action in a all conclusive manner. The Audit Wing of Head Office will be
specifically communicating the dropping of observations based on qualifying. replies and
the communication of HO must be attached to the IAR concerned for future reference.

circular No.Pen,/Misc/2006/44884 dated 21.09.2006 are not being strictly complied

Sub:-Critical Appraisal of claim settlement vis-a-vis EPFO Mandate.

E.P.F.O. has been mandated to extend and manage old-age income security
programs and it has to carry out dual role of Regulator and Service Provider of
Provident Fund, Pension and Deposit Linked Insurance Schemes, for largest number of
workers in India. For this purpose, it has to carry out various activities such as coverage
of establishments detection of evasion, determination and collection of dues, investment
of funds, settlement of claims, updation of members account etc.

With increasing job migrations over last few years, claim settlement activity has
increased phenomenally and it has overshadowed all other activities of the Organisation.
The ever increasing volume of claims has compeiled us to divert ali our resources to this
activity. In view of unusually high volume of claims, an analysis of claim settlement
figures was carried out at Sub-Regional Office, Karnal. This analysis has revealed
stunning facts and a few are cited below:

> 88.89% of the EPF claims pertain to category wherein reason of leaving service is
“resignation”.

46.5% persons get up to meager Rs.10,000/- as PF settlement.

Payment to mere 4.2% subscribers is above Rs.1 lac.

30.2% subscriber withdraws P.F. within 1 year of service and this figure reaches
54.3% by the end of 2™ year. .

Age of 37.9% subscribers, at the time of P.F. withdrawal is up to 30 years only.
Majority of claimants withdraw their P.F. balance with every job change.

Mere 5.82% subscribers render minimum service of 10 years, primary eligibility
condition for pension.

VV WwW

VvWv

These facts are indicative of highly inflated workload of claim settlement on
account of pre-mature withdrawal. Not only that, the very purpose of EPF & MP Act 1952
has been defeated as only a minuscule portion of subscribers have sufficient balance in
PF account at the time of superannuation.

The analysis carried out at SRO, Karnal indicates an immediate need of legislative
changes to contain pre-mature withdrawals. However, before we move ahead in that

direction, there is a need to broaden the data base, to arrive at a representative sample
of population. It has been decided to carry out this analysis for your office also. For this
purpose, detailed guidelines on ‘how to carry out the analysis is enclosed. Analysis
paper prepared by SRO, Karnal is also enclosed for your ready reference. You are
required to go through these directions carefully and carry out the analysis. The analysis
must be completed and mailed electronically to jainoida@yahoo.com_ latest _b

31.12.2010. For any clarifications on carrying out this analysis, you may contact RPFC,
Karnal at 09467800700.

Timeline must be strictly adhered to.

Dear Commissioner 5 DEC 2010

Please refer to our letter No. RRC-II/28(26)06/ABR dated the 25" November,
2010 directing for Special Recovery Drive and Special Coverage Drive. The object
of the drive is to make good the deficiency in coverage of establishments,
membership and recovery of assessed amount. The recovery collection is most
unsatisfactory. The overall recovery in unexempted sector is only 17% whereas in
exempted sector it is only 14.7%. Similarly assessment is also one of the neglected
areas.

2. We have vast powers to recover the dues and take stringent action against
defaulters. Prosecution may be effective tool to deal the chronic defaulters.

3. However, the report reveals that 17 Regional Offices have not filed even a
single prosecution during the year 2009-10.

4. Status of 406/409 IPC cases is equally bad.

5. During the last year 174 cases of 406/409 IPC were dropped by Police.

6. | fail to understand as to how these cases could be dropped. Under law, case
of breach of trust once committed cannot be dropped. It indicates that we failed to
provide relevant information/evidence to the Police about the commission of offence.
7. All the Regional PF Commissioners should ensure that in no circumstances

such cases are dropped. Under Section 14 A B offence relating to default in
payment of contributions by the employer punishable under the Act, is cognizable

offence. The cognizable offence is offence where the police is empowered to arrest
without warrant.

8. Considering the huge default and poor recovery, | am constrained to direct
that this law must be invoked against major and chronic defaulters by filing
F.I.Rs to Police and ensuring prompt action by Police.

9. It must be noted that this is not a tool for harassment and may not be invoked
against small employers.

10. | am also looking forward for the pro-active action for converting the Not
immediately releasable (NIR) Arrear into Realisable demand, and recover the dues
as already directed by letter dated 25.11.2010 referred above.

11. The Legal department should also act promptly in enquiry cases and avoiding
stay of operation by Court. A Legal Counsel/Officer to argue cases at admission
stage itself should be appointed for each court. Please assign specific tasks to the
Officials in your Office and monitor them regularly.

11. The current situation of inaction is not acceptable. If the desired results are
not visible, action against all non performers will have to be initiated. You are also
advised to take action against such non-performers under you.

12. | would request you to consolidate the report and send the Zonal Reports by

15" January, 2011, indicating the action taken under Assessment, Recovery and

Legal, Prosecutions under Section 14, filing of FiRs and action for arrest etc. as

already indicated vide letter No. RRC-II/28(26) ABR dated 25" November, 2010.

Sub:- Proposal for Compassionate Appointment-regarding.
Sir,

As you are aware that consequent upon re-structuring in the various cadre of
Information Service Division the cadre of Data Processing Assistant in the pay band
of Rs, .9300- 34800 was introduced in place of Data Entry Operators. The cadre of
Data Entry Operators has been declared as dying cadre. Therefore, compassionate

appointment in the cadre of DEO can not be considered.

As a consequence of the implementation of VI th Central Pay Commission by
Govt. the Ministry of Finance (Department of Expenditure) vide its “Office Circular
F. No. 1/1/2008-1C dated 24.12.2008 has stated that “all existing Group ‘D’
employees are required to be upgraded to the pre-revised Group’C’ scale of Rs. 27504400 corresponding to the grade pay of Rs. 1800 in PB-1 (Rs. 5200-20200) in the
manner prescribed in the CCS (Revised Pay) Rules, 2008, which prescribes the
procedure for fixation of pay of Group ‘D’ employees in the revised pay structure.
Further it is also mentioned that in future, posts will be created only in PB-1 and
there shall be no recruitment in IS pay band save in exceptional circumstances as
indicated in pare 02.02.10 of the Report of the Six Central Pay Commission Keeping
in view the provision of said rule, the steps have been taken to adopt the model
recruitment rules to the post of Multi-Tasking Staff in EPFO as applicable to

counterparts in Government. The action for framing the recruitment rules of Multi

Tasking Staff (Gr. C) has been initiated and after completion of the process further
action will be taken. uO

Therefore in view of above the cases of compassionate appointment to the
post of Data Entry Operator received from Regional offices are returned separately.
Accordingly the proposal for compassionate appointment in respect of the
applicants may be examined afresh in the light of the recruitment rules of Social
Securing Assistant, and submit your proposal to head office for specific post after

judging the suitability of the applicant for the said post for consideration.

Thus at present compassionate appointment could be considered only in the
post of Social Security Assistant as per rules and eligibility criteria. All regions are,

therefore, requested to process cases of Compassionate Appointment accordingly.

Sub.: Enrolment of workers engaged in Building and Construction
Industries-— reg.

Sir,

The Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and
Conditions of Service) Act, 1996 came into force from 19-08-1996. Under Section 7 of
this Act, every employer on which this Act applies requires to be registered within a
period of sixty days from its commencement by making an application to the Registering
Officer. Similarly, every building worker of 18 to 60 years of age and working for not
less than 90 days during the preceding 12 months is also eligible for registration as a
beneficiary under this Act. Also vide section 4 of this Act, a State Advisory Committee
is required to be constituted by the State Government to advise on the matters arising
out of the administration of the Act.

In addition to the above, according to Building and other Construction Workers
Welfare Cess Act, 1996, Rule 7, the employer is required to submit information in Form-I
which inter-alia contains details of commencement of work, number of workers
employed etc. Head Office had issued earlier instruction to utilize the information from
these sources for coverage and detect evasion.

The Sub-Committee of CBT on Construction Workers desires to have a
comparative statement of employees covered under the EPF & MP Act, 1952 and
number of employees registered with the State Advisory Committee in order to know the
extent of evasion under the Act. Therefore, you are requested to depute the EO and
collect the details from the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board and
forward to this office in the following format :

Software would be eligible for Honorarium @ ZTI rates. Some offices however have

field offices. Accordingly, it is clarified that all such trainers are eligible for honorarium as

Sub: Launching of Special Recovery Drive and Special Coverage Drive —
December, 2010.

Sir,

It has been time and again impressed upon in various review meeting and
also conveyed through a number of communications sent by the Head Office that
the task of coverage and recovering Provident Fund dues should be accorded
due priority but the pace of coverage and recoveries made during this financial
year reveals that due importance is not given to coverage and realization of
arrears. The review of organizations performance reveals that the Organization
has been able to recover only 16.5% of the outstanding dues upto September,
2010. The share of recoveries against current demand is 49% of the current
workload whereas the recoveries against arrear demand stand to a poor 7% of
the Arrear workload.

Similarly, is has been noticed that social security benefits are not being
extended to large number of employees working in certain industries even where
the establishments are covered under the Act.

Central Provident fund Commissioner is not satisfied with the performance
in various compliance areas. It appears that no sincere efforts are taken by the
field offices on their initiation. Even the commands from Head Office are not
penetrating and lost attention after a short period. )

The Compliance is not limited to simply coverage that to only issuing code
numbers. Accordingly, following actions must be taken as a special drive to
accomplish the task in a time bound manner

(i) Launch coverage drive to cover all coverable establishment:

(ii) Initiation of 7A proceedings in all cases of defaults

(iii) | Finalised the 7A proceedings within 6 months from the date of
initiation

(iv) Enrolment of all eligible members in covered/coverable
establishments. .

(v) Recovery of current demand invoking all the powers vested with
officer

(vi) Recover 80% arrears demand

(vii) Ensure to unlock all the blocked up arrears by approaching
appropriate courts for vacation of stay etc.

(viii) Filing prosecution under Section 14 in respect of all defaulters
without fail. This will be one of the major strategies for recovery.

In view of the above, it has been decided to observe the month of
December, 2010 as “Total Compliance” to set this task in forefront. It has to
be ensured that performance improvement is visible.

It is also emphasized that the big defaulters should be proceeded against
first and then come down to the smaller defaulter.

It is once again emphasized that focused and pro-active steps should be
taken to ensure the recovery as per the targets including special efforts in
unlocking the not immediately realizable demand. This has to be achieved
through special efforts initiated for getting the stay orders vacated, moving
special petitions for early hearing of pending cases, getting claims, expeditiously
settled from the official liquidators and such other actions required depending on
the merits of individual cases. Repeat and habitual defaulters should be targeted
first for recovery.

You are therefore directed to advise RPFCs under your jurisdiction to take
necessary action by constituting squads of Enforcement Officers who will take up
extensive visits to all the probable industries / units where evasion / noncoverage has been reported.

Progress report of the coverage month may be forwarded by 15.1.2011. In
other area also regular and effective monitoring is required at all levels and the
performance parameters should indicate improvements.

(This is issued as directed by Central PF Commissioner )

Yours faithfully,

Subject: - Entering of mobile numbers in the application software for SMS facilities ~ reg

As we are all aware, the centralised SMS service launched in July 2010, was done based on the principle of
acknowledging any claim form submitted by a member / subscriber and updating him/her about the status as
well as the final settlement details of same.

Keeping this basic requirement in mind, provision for entering mobile numbers in the new application
software has been incorporated and a facility for settling a claim through NEFT which is fast and cost effective
was introduced. Necessary instructions were also issued to all the field offices to ensure that mobile numbers
are furnished in the claim forms and also they are entered in the application software invariably. To ensure
smooth flow of information on daily basis, provision for uploading / sending the data to NDC servers on daily
basis has also been provided.

However, the overall performance of this service so far is abysmal and highly disheartening. The dashboard
depicting the number of SMSs sent is monitored by CPFC himself and he has expressed his extreme
displeasure in various review meetings. This is very badly reflecting on the overall performance of the Project
and IS Divisions of Head Office and threatening the very existence of the SMS service which has been
introduced with a cause.

As of now the main reason for the above cited state of affairs is the absence of mobile numbers in the data. So
far field offices were taking the stance that they are settling the pending claims which were having no mobile
numbers. However, it is more than three months now and competent authorities are not buying this argument

anymore.

| would like to draw the personal attention of the RPFCs/ OICs, in this regard and | request them to ensure that
the following instructions are strictly followed henceforth:

1. The Receipt clerk / Dealing Assistant enters the mobile number furnished by the claimant in
application software. To make it mandatory, provision for entering the same at receipt level itself has
been introduced in the application software (Ver 2.40). If, the mobile number is not furnished, they
have to enter the default number (1234567890) which internally mean “Mobile No. NOT furnished” on
the claim form. An MIS report will be taken based on this criteria and if it is found that mobile
numbers were not entered in spite of the fact that it is present on the claim form, it will be viewed
very seriously and necessary action will be taken against the Receipt clerk / DA.

2. The performance of all the offices are being monitored through dashboard and the list of offices not
sending data on daily basis are furnished to the competent authority for further necessary action. All
offices should ensure that the mobile data files for NEFT payment and the claim status data files are

uploaded daily without fail. As there is no reason why the files cannot be uploaded on daily basis, no

laxity in this regard will be tolerated.
For strict compliance and implementation by all field offices without fail.

This issues with the approval of CPFC.

Bal,

(B.K. Panda)

A review of Court cases of EPFO reveals that a large no. of cases are
pending before various courts. In certain cases, the matters are sub-judice for
years together. While non-representation and lack of pursuit on the part of EPFO
is one of the reasons for pendency, the huge backlog with the respective Courts

setting up of Special Courts and Special Benches has therefore, been felt for
expediting the disposal of our cases under litigation. The Petition Committee of
Lok Sabha has also emphasized on this issue.

High Courts of your State/Region for setting up Special Courts/ Special Benches
for hearing EPFO cases. While taking up the issue, the social security aspect and

Sir,

The result of the EO/AO examination held from 7" to 11 December, 2009 was
announced for 13 candidates as against 15 vacancies due to OA.No. 615/2009 of CAT,
Jabalpur bench.

The applicants in this OA, Deepak Kulkarni, Deepak Tomar & Rajendra Singh
Yadav, (all three are SSAs) were not eligible (as on 1.1.2009), as per recruitment rules to
apply for the EO/AO Departmental examination for promotion. However, they were
allowed due to the interim order of the CAT. The results were not declared as the
candidates were not eligible as per recruitment rules and the decision was pending.

The said OA is dismissed by the CAT vide its order dated 22.10.2010. The Hon'ble
CAT has observed and ordered that:

“Since the applicants were clearly ineligible to appear in the examination, we hold that the
respondents are not bound to declare the results of the applicants and the respondents are free
to declare the results of other eligible candidates who had appeared in the said examination and
the respondents can go ahead with the process of promotion as a result of the final result of the
impugned examination. Though the applicants were permitted, by way of the interim relief, to
appear in the impugned examination, yet on account of the decision in this OA, the respondents
are not required to declare their results, as they were clearly ineligible to appear in the impugned
examination.

In view of above reasons, the present OA is dismissed with no order as to costs.”

The marks of all candidates who appeared for the EO/AO Examination were given
vide letter No.Exam.5.(1)/2009/428 dated 5/13.8.2010. The following two candidates
come at the 14" & 15™ position in merit order under General Category in Madhya
Pradesh. They are now declared successful in the EO/AO Departmental competitive
examination for promotion against the examination conducted from 7" to 11 December,
2009.

. Central provident Fund Commissioner has directed that a comprehensive
compliance audit of all exempted establishments (u/s 17(1)(a)/para 79 or para 27A)
shall be carried out by all offices between 08.11.10 and 31.12.10. The compliance audit

should cover the period till 31.03.10.

and submitted to their office for further necessary action.

a Officer in charge shall ensure that the Compliance Audit is completed in a time
bound manner by forming sufficient number of squads so that all the establishments are
inspected by 31.12.10. It shall be the responsibility of the officer in charge to ensure
that the inspecting teams are properly briefed and their tour programmes are approved
well in advance so that the time lines are strictly adhered.

to Head Office are incomplete particularly where the P.F trust of the establishment is
located outside the jurisdiction of the concerned RPFC. In such cases the officer in

establishment or a reference be sent to the concerned RPFC in whose jurisdiction the

trust is located to inspect the records of the trust and submit the required information in
a time bound manner. Under no circumstances incomplete report should be submitted
by the squad. It is also clarified that the Compliance audit is to be conducted both in
respect of the establishment as well as on its P.F Trust, hence a through inspection of
all relevant records should be made before recording the observations in the proforma
(Annexure-l).

Sub:- Claim Settlement-alerts through SMS — awareness —reg.

Sir,

As you may be aware of the features of providing claim settlement —
alerts through SMS to members has been provided both in the new application
and the legacy application. Instructions were also given to obtain the mobile
numbers of subscribers in the claim application forms.

While there has been a marginal improvement in the number of sms
alerts being sent, there is a large scope of improving the situation. Officers in
charge of respective offices should take all the necessary measures to increase
awareness of the facility among member. It has been decided to fix a target of at
least 50% claims to be processed with mobile numbers by end of this month.

In addition, all RCs and OlCs are requested to ensure hundred percent
entry of mobile nos. while settling the claims at receipt — level. To make this
facility known to more members, it was suggested to give it wide publicity. One
step which has been taken by the SRO Jabalpur is that they have prepared flex
board of 2’x2’ and 2’x3’ sizes and displayed it in Banks and ATMs after
discussing with various banks for free of costs. This has yielded very good
results. You are requested to explore this at your end so that more people can
come to know of this and provide their mobile nos. Atleast 60% of the claims
settled by your office should have members mobile no. by the end of this month.

Yours faithfully

Sub: Stray Instances of Dishonor of Cheques

Ref : (i) This Office letter No. Bkg.1(5)2006/Agreement/Part dtd. 12.04.2010
(ii)This Office letter No. Bkg.1(5)2006/Agreement/Part/2026 dtd. 29.04.2010
Sir,

Instances have come to the notice of Head Office on dishonor of cheques at
different Regional and Sub Regional Offices. The issue was taken up with State Bank
of India on 01.10.2010 while signing the Banking Agreement. The Central Provident
Fund Commissioner has expressed his Concern on such dishonor of cheques. To
overcome the situation, following instructions are issued for strict compliance:

1. All the Officers in Charge of Regional and Sub Regional offices shall closely
monitor the Fund position with the Link Branches of State bank of India
under their jurisdiction in Account No.l and Account No.10 on daily basis
and to draw a strategy so that the cheques issued by them are within the
overdraft limit allowed.

2. Since the quantum of cheques issued and amount to be debited on
account of such cheques are available with Regional and Sub Regional
Offices, it should be ensured that while issuing fresh cheques the position of
cheques issued but not presented at the bank and the amounts involved
therein should be monitored in such a way that there is no dishonor of
cheques.

3. The trend of debits from Account No. 1 & 10 may be evaluated on monthly
basis and while doing so, if there occurs the need for enhancing the
overdraft limit at the respective Link Branches, the matier may be taken
up with State Bank Of India locally.

sete

a

—Z4. All the Officers in Charge of Regional and Sub Regional offices shall
maintain continuous co-ordination with State Bank of India locally so that
dishonor of EPFO cheques are avoided for want of funds.

5. It is the responsibility of the Regional and Sub Regional Offices to have
appropriate interaction with the Link Branches of State Bank of India. If at
all, any problem is anticipated and not addressable locally, the matter
may be reported to ACC(Zones) for further taking Up the issue at the level
of CGM/GM, Circle-in-charge.

6. APFC(Cash) is primarily responsible if any cheque is dishonored and
overall responsibility lies with RPFC-II(Finance & Accounts) in case of
Regional Office and RPFC-II & O-I-C in case of Sub Regional Offices.

The instances of dishonor of cheques will be viewed seriously and the
matter will be placed before the Competent Authority for fixing of
accountability.

Yours faithfully,

Regional P.F. Commissioner-!

Sub.: Inspection and Assessment of dues of establishments engaged
in construction activities - reg.
Sir,

Kindly refer to the subject cited above. You are aware that the
establishments engaged in Building and Construction activity was brought
under the purview of the Act w.e.f 31% October, 1980. In order to identify the
establishments, the provisions contained in the Building and other
construction workers (Regulation of Employment and conditions of Service)
Act 1996 which came into force w.e.f 19" August, 1996, may also be
utilized for collecting the details including the names of the workers
employed in the industry.

Accordingly the establishments engaged in building and constructions
activities are required to be identified and covered under the EPF & MP Act
1952 and social security benefits to be provided to the employees / workers
as per provision contained therein.

Now, a grave deficiency in assessment of dues u/s 7A of the Act has
been pointed out by the CVO, HQ in case of such establishments which may
have a general trend of occurrence. During the course of investigating a
complaint regarding a construction establishment, It was found that in case
of large Construction Companies handling multiple projects, the assessment
of dues are not made taking into account all the projects of the
establishment. It may lead to huge under assessment and. in turn non
extension of social security coverage to all entitled employees engaged at
different project sites. It is a serious irregularity and deficiency on the part of
Assessing Officer. The role of Supervisory Officials also can not be ignored.
Therefore, in view of findings of the Vigilance and to avoid recurrence of such
instances it is directed that:

(1) Inspections should be carried out regularly,

(2)

(3)

(4)

(5)

The squads /EOs deputed should invariably inspect the Balance sheet,
Books of accounts etc of the establishment covering all the units and
Head Office of the concerned establishment,

The Assessing officer should apply his mind and consider full details /
records for assessment of dues and before accepting the EO’s Report
and relying on it for assessment of dues.

The supervisory officer should follow the regular supervisory checks
on the conduct and quality of 7A orders.

Strict action to be initiated against the EOs submitting incomplete and
deficient reports as well as other Officers involved.

It is, therefore, directed that these directions should be scrupulously

followed for assessment of dues u/s 7A of the Act as well as while conducting
~ the inspection of all establishments especially with multiple projects. ~° ---—---

Sub: Roll out of 'Computerisation Project' — Commencement of Parallel Run Go-Live
activities from 30th September, 2010.
Sir,
The 58 offices comprising the second tier for implementation of the
'Computerization Project' have registered considerable progress in the preparatory work as
per the scheduled plan for implementation to commence from September 30 th, 2010.
It has been felt prudent that the implementation of the project in each office should
commence with a parallel run of one to four weeks depending upon the readiness of the
offices in respect to the availability of required infrastructure & appropriate level of
competence & knowledge amongst the staff, during which the personnel are fully
familiarized with operations in the new system with local data, followed by the Go-Live
where complete operations of the office are carried out solely in the new system.
The new application software with the enabling operating systems should be
installed before 30th September, 2010 with the help of technical manpower deployed in
your office and with the aid of other senior technical persons available in your zone. Before
the launch and during the countdown all the offices are required to submit daily progress
report to headquarters.

In order to start the Parallel run in the 58 offices from 30 th September 2010, the
following strategy for the parallel is delineated for implementation:
Data Migration for commencement of Parallel Run
The parallel run will commence from 30 th September 2010 and will continue for one
to four weeks depending upon the situation of each office. In this phase, Legacy data in
respect of the Establishments having more than 100 accounts shall be released for
establishment as a whole after verifying the correctness of the summary data from Form
24 on the screen. Data in respect of the remaining establishments will be released without
verification. The Data Migration process should be computed within one week. At this
stage, certification of the legacy data will not be required. Claim settlement process and
other activities will not be closed during this period of 4 weeks.
During the parallel run certain activities such as settlement of claims, reconciliation
of receipt and payment, closing of cash book, compilation of annual statement of accounts
etc. are required to be done on the legacy system as well as in the new application
software.
During this phase of the parallel run, broadly the following activities need to be
performed:-
Creation of users, Task mapping, and Establishment Master will be released. Field
office Masters will be authenticated by the respective offices.
Legacy establishment challans data will be released on need basis on the screen.
Legacy PPO data will be released based upon last approved BRS. However 100 PPO per
Dealing assistant will be verified from actual PPO files and time taken for verification from
the PPO file need to be recorded.
Data will be migrated to the new system and cross tallied with the check totals
generated from the DMCC software as well as Data transfer software including number of
records in each table and bytes table wise shall be recorded.
Claims are required to be received after embossing receipt stamp on the claim form
and acknowledgement be given to the claimant. Such claims should be entered in the
legacy system as well as in the new application software.
Handling of Claims during the parallel run
Claims receipt will be processed in the legacy system as well as in the new
application software. Receipt number of the legacy system should be recorded on the
claim forms as usual. System generated acknowledgement slip in the new system will be
attached with the claim form.
Claims worksheet first will be generated from CCPS software in legacy and
thereafter in the new system.
Printing of worksheet is to be done in the account

Sub: Submission of Revised Estimates for the year 2010-11 and Budget
Estimates for the year 2011-12 in respect of Employees' Provident Fund
Scheme, 1952 (including Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995) and
Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme, 1976.
In accordance with the provisions contained in Para 58 of the EPF
Scheme 1952 on Budget, on probable Receipts and Expenditure relating to
the Administration of the Funds, the Revised Estimates for the year 2010-11 and
the Budget Estimates for the year 2011-12 of the EPF Organisation, based on
the actual Income & Expenditure upto 30th September 2010 (i.e. from 1.4.2010
to 30.9.2010), are to be prepared and placed before the Central Board of
Trustees, for the consideration and approval in this financial year. For smooth
and timely preparation of the Revised Estimates for 2010-11 and Budget
Estimates for 2011-12, the following general instructions are issued for
guidance.
2.
The budgetary exercise should not be treated as mere routine and it
should receive the personal attention of the Regional Commissioner and the
OIC of SRO both for its correctness and timely submission. On the part of the
RPFC (F&A), it should be treated as a vital function for the respective Region
including for the SROs and he should devote his personal attention in assisting
the Regional Commissioner in-charge of the Region. Efforts should be made to
frame the Revised Estimates for 2010-11 in such a manner that there may not
be any necessity for Re-appropriation/ Additional Funds in the last months of
the financial year.

3.
The NATRSS is treated as an independent unit and separate funds are
allotted to meet its own expenditure and the Zonal Training Institutes '(ZTIs),
Sub-ZTI (Shillong) working under .-them. As such, Director, NATRSS, will submit
Budget Proposal separately for NATRSS and ZTIs including Sub-ZTI (Shillong).
Budget for Deputy Director, Vigilance (NZ) may be included in the BE for
NATRSS.
4.
Similarly, the EPF Appellate Tribunal has also been treated as a separate
unit and separate funds are to be allotted to meet its own expenditure. As
such, Registrar, EPF Appellate Tribunal will also submit budget proposal
separately.
5.
The following guidelines may please be kept in mind while formulating
the Revised Estimates for 2010-11 and Budget Estimates for 2011-12: -
(I) One single proposal is required to be prepared in respect of a Region as
a whole by consolidating the proposals of Regional Office and the SubRegional Offices. RPFC-In-Charge of the Region as well as RPFC-II(F&A)
may therefore get in touch with the OlCs of Sub-Regional Offices under
their control immediately to ensure that there is no delay in transmission
of the requisite information to their office. The Revised Estimates for
2010-11 and Budget Estimates for 2011-12 for the offices of Addl. CPFCs
(Political States) and Permanent Inquiry Officers, Zonal Audit Parties and
Deputy Directorates (Vigilance) may include their new requirements, if
any, other then the routine items like Pay & allowances, TA, Stationary,
Phone, Fax bills etc. to the Regional Offices or NATRSS whichever is
concerned; where these offices are situated, which in turn, will include
the same in the consolidated budget proposal of the Region.
(ii) With a view to enable us to assess the amount of contributions
estimated as receivable during the year 2010-11 (Revised Estimates)
and in 2011-12 (Budget Estimates), the details of contributions may be
given in Statements as prescribed in Annexure - BT/A.

Sir,

In pursuance of the decision of the Executive Committee, CBT,

EPF in its 56" meeting to empanel reputed Movers & Packers to defray the cost

of relocation of officials having all India Transfer Liability on their transfer in lieu

of payment of freight charges, sealed quotations were invited from reputed

Packers & Movers having all India presence. On scrutiny of quotations, 02

Movers & Packers viz M/s. OM Logistics Ltd. & M/s. Golden Packers & Movers

Pvt. Ltd. are empanelied for this purpose. A copy of the signed agreement with

these two companies is uploaded on the official website of EPFO. '

Z. Under this arrangement the consignment shall be loaded from the
residence of the concerned transferred official and shall be delivered at
the address declared by the official. The party shall pack and unpack the
items of the consignment at the address given by the official using the
service.

3. The charges quoted by Packers & Movers shall include charges for pre
survey, cost of good quality of packing material required (like corrugated,

bubble, thermocole, polythene, cartons and necessary allied material,

10.

crating of fragile items, stretch films, strapping, taping, gluing with
stickering and escort), charges for packing by expert and trained packers,
complete documentation, loading, transportation, unpacking at the delivery
point and removal of debris.

The charges quoted shall be exclusive of insurance charges, service tax
and all other government levies, which would be paid on actual basis on
submission of original receipt as provided in the agreement.

Payment will be made on case to case basis from the EPFO field office
under whose jurisdiction the consignment is delivered on production of
work orders issued by EPF office, bill along with satisfactory performance
reports from the users of the services. The payment would be subject to
Tax Deductions at Source as per rate prescribed under relevant

Government Rules.

This arrangement would be from 07.09.2010 to 06.09.2011 for period of

one year. This agreement may be extended subject to satisfactory
performance/services on mutually agreed terms.

This arrangement is not mandatory and officials have the option either to
use this arrangement or make their own arrangements to transport their
personal effects and in such cases bills/claims shall be regulated as per
FR/SR Rules applicable to the official of E.P.F. Organisation.

EPFO would not be legally responsible for any damage /deficiency of
service, etc.

Sub: -
Allotment of Code Number - Reg.
Allotment of Code Number to the establishments is an administrative
process of registering an establishment through a code number to link up the
remittances made by it with reference to its employees and to maintain their
proper accounts including extension of service delivery to the members.
( 1 )
Time for Allotment of Code Number:-
The process of allotment of code number has been modified from
time to time as per requirement of the field offices, the industrial and economic
scenario of the country and introduction of IT.
_The three days time period for allotment -of---code number was
introduced under Compliance 2001 Programme. However, over a period of
time, it has become a point of major concern for increase in fly-by-night
establishments. The field offices have been indicating that the three days time
period is not sufficient to verify the genuineness of the coverage application as
well as the information provided in it. It has led to increase in the in-operative
accounts and increased work load in terms of maintenance of accounts of such
establishments which do not comply subsequently but continue to be reflected
in the workload.
(a)
In view of above, it is decided that the processing time for
coverage application by the office shall be allowed to be two weeks or
a maximum of 10 working days from the date of the receipt of
coverage proposal.
(b)
Before allotment of code number, there should be a mandatory
inspection to verify the address and
, other relevant details of the
establishment/Employer and all its employees. Attempt should be
made to obtain official, residential and permanent address of the
employer/directors/proprietors along with any of valid identity proofs
e.g. PAN card, voters id, passport etc. and which has to be updated
on subsequent inspections.
(c)
The EO should also verify the Identity details of all the employees.
This verification of the employees of the establishment should be with
reference to their valid identify proof like; Voters ID Card, Ration
Card, ESIC Card, Pass Book, Driving Licence or any other such proof
of identification issued by any Government body.
(d)
However, in cases where officer concerned is satisfied (for reasons
recorded in writing) with the information and documents furnished
with the coverage application; code number can be allotted forthwith
with post coverage inspection within three months from the allotment
of code number.

Sub.: Provision of generator set and modular furniture in the rental
buildings.

Sir,

Please refer to this office letter No. Adm. (R.111)3/2/94/Pt/Generator/KN
DATED 1.02.1996. It appears that owing to the provision for modular furniture
and generator sets, the computerization work scheduled to be rolled out in
your offices working in the rental building is not progressing satisfactorily. In
this regard, it is clarified as under: -

(1) The IS Division and PED have issued clear guidelines for the field
offices operating the rental facility may hire the generator set observing
the appropriate guidelines and it should not be a barrier in
implementation of the project computerization. Authority Circular letter
No. Adm.(R.111)3(2)/94/Pt./Generator/KN dated 1.02.1996. However, it
is stated that PFD is expediting with the Finance Division to ensure that
all the offices in the rental premises are provided with approval to
purchase the generator set against the specified capacity (SRO — 70
KVA, RO -— 120 KVA).

(2) It has been seen from the previous experience that while first leg
computerization was done at 28 stations: offices did successfully
computerization itself in the locations where modular furniture was still
not installed. Even though we are putting all out efforts to get
sanctions for the rental building for modular furniture, however, all
rental offices need proper signed legal agreement and owners No
Objection being a pre-requisite for the execution of AC/modular
furniture. You are advised to act on it simyltaneously if not done so far.

pun feat 4 cara ar ee 4 wa wal we GET onag A ut 1

(3) About modular furniture, necessary processing has been done at Head
Office level and appropriate orders communicating the approval will be
shared with all such offices that are running into rental premises as
soon as possible. It is pertinent to mention that availability of modular
furniture is not a pre-condition for computerization and all of you are
advised that the electrical cabling, laying of LAN and other work should
be continued keeping in mind that may be after some time the
necessary approval for procurement of modular furniture may be
accorded and for the same necessary communication shall follow.

(4) The provision of air-conditioning is essential only for the server room.
You may refer the delegated powers under “Office Equipment’ wherein
RCs have been given the power of Rs. One lac and ACC upto Rs. Two
lacs and various offices did purchase the ACs under such powers.
Essential air-conditioning for server room should not be a barrier
needing any clearance from Headquarters. However, to create an
enabling work environment, the Headquarter is considering to accord
approval for air-conditioning of the different offices for which the PFD,
IS and Finance Division are coordinating to get standardized guidelines
issued as soon as possible.

Conclusively, it may be noted that in the light of above facts, all of you
should initiate action and ensure that on account of non-availability of
generator set (on purchase basis) and modular furniture should not be treated
as a problem in launching the project computerization in your office by 30" of
September 2010 . Your urgent intermediation and execution of these
guidelines is solicited. We further wish to clarify that necessary approval for
the Generator Set, Modular furniture and Air-conditioning with required
guidelines shall be issued.

Yours faithfully,

Sub: Stepping up of pay of Assistants (re-designated as Sr. SSA) at par with their juniors
who were promoted as Sr. SSA (TBP) under Time Bound Promotion Scheme on
completion of 17 years clerical serviceSir,
On the basis of representations received from several Regions, and from All India
EPF Staff Federation for removal of pay anomaly arisen due to grant of pay scale of
Rs.5500-9000 to Sr. Social Security Assistant (TBP) who were promoted under Time
Bound Promotion Scheme on completion of 17 years' of clerical service and in the pay of
Assistant [re-designated as Sr. Social Security Assistant)] being senior to Sr. Social
Security Assistant(TBP) but continued in the pay scale of 5000-8000 (pre-revised).
2.
The matter has been examined in consultation with Finance Wing of Head office and
keeping in view the instructions of DOP & T, the Competent Authority is pleased to approve
the stepping up of pay of seniors (Sr. Social Security Assistant) to bring it at par with their
juniors [Sr. Social Security Assistant (TBP) as on 31.03.2004]. Pay will be fixed under Rule
FR 22(1)(a)(2) w.e.f. 01.04.2004 notionally and financial benefits are payable w.e.f.
01.09.2007 i.e. from the date from which Sr. Social Security Assistant(TBP) were given the
monetary benefits under the up-graded scale of Rs. 5500-9000 (pre-revised).
3.
All Regional P. F. Commissioner's are therefore requested to allow stepping up in
such cases where Assistants (now, Sr. Social Security Assistant) are drawing less pay than
their juniors [Sr. Social Security Assistant (TBP] accordingly. The compliance report may
please be furnished to this office on or before 30th Sep. 2010.

Sub: Training on computerization project — Reg.
Sir,

As we are aware application software is to be made operational in 58 offices.
Training of officials constitutes an important input in this direction for successful
implementation.

To provide more understanding of application software, it has been decided to
provide familirazation with the new application sotware to the officials of 2" tier
offices.

Officer-incharge of 2™ tier offices will select one SSA each from the Accounts
and Cash & Pension wings and send to the nearest 28 offices which have already been
go live in 1* tier (training schedule enclosed) keeping in mind that these persons have
to guide the other staff in their sections when the Project is launched in their own
office. However following guidelines are to be followed for this training:-

(1) The accounts personnel will sit in the Accounts Branch of the
computerized office and observe the way processing is being done in the
computerized office.

(2) The staff from cash and pension wing will sit in the respective cash and
pension wing to learn the processes of those sections.

(3) Some of the offices that are big such as Bandra, may send the persons in
two or three batches in consultation with the concerned office where staff
are to be sent.

(4) The computerized office will allow these staff to sit in the respective
sections along with an SSA or SS to let them see the processes and try to
give the necessary exposure and guidence. |

(5) If possible an officer may also address the visitors informing them about
the essential details of the application software.

(6) The training/familiarization programme will be of 3 days and will start
from 30" August 2010.

(7) This familiarization programme are in addition to the instructions send
vide letter no. R-I/Training/2009 dated 11.08.2010 for end user training
at your Office.

This may please be treated as urgent.

Yours faithfully

Pevqacd,

Sub.: Combating Corruption- Need for greater Vigilance- regarding.

EPFO being, both, a public services delivery organization and a law enforcement
agency has, naturally a wide public interface. It should, therefore be an organizational
endeavor to ensure highest standards of service delivery at all times while refusing to make
any compromise whatsoever with the interests of the multiple stake- holders. However, of
late, recurrent instances of corruption have constituted a blot on the image and reputation
of the organization. It is even more distressing to note that the incidents of trap and other
corruption cases shows no signs of abatement and even senior officers have been found to
be booked by CBI and other Anti-Corruption Bureaus in various cases. Needless to say
such instances lower the Organization’s reputation as a whole and all the EPFO
functionaries run the risk of being tarred with the same brush. This cancer of corruption can

be ignored only at our own peril.

It is seen that such unpalatable incidents often have their genesis in the reluctance on
the part of the supervisory officers to ensure that the safeguards built into the system are
not subverted. There is a marked tendency among even senior officers to play a passive
role when confronted with the challenge of combating corruption. It is conveniently
perceived that this job is the responsibility of the Vigilance Wing alone and only when
complaints are formally lodged the administrative authorities are supposed to take action
of any kind. It is high time that this misconception is dispelled and it is emphasized
that the Supervisory Authorities constitute the first line of defence against the onslaught

Cont. 2

2


of corruption.  Effective Supervision at all levels would thwart any attempt at mischief
and ensure that efficient service is available at each point of delivery.

In this context, it would be worth reminding ourselves that it is not the case that we
do  not  have  proper  procedures  and  practices.  Nor  is  it  that  there  exists  any  ambiguity
regarding the duties and responsibilities of each post in the organization.  The Manual of
Accounting  Procedure‐Part‐I  (General)  lays  down  the  duties  and  responsibilities  of  the
various functionaries and the same are well defined.  These are further supplemented by
various  administrative  instructions  for  regulating  the  work  flow  and  optimizing
performance.  This is especially the case as regards the functioning of the Compliance and
Recovery wings of the Organization. There have been instructions issued time to time on
the subject including   exercise of quasi‐judicial powers under section 7A of the Act and
section  14B  of  the  Act.    Therefore  it  is  self  evident  that  the  system  has  not  failed  us  but
rather it is we who have failed the system.
With  a  view  to  ensure  greater  involvement  and  accountability  of  the  various
supervisory authorities the following measures are directed to be taken at all relevant levels:

A.) COMPLIANCE:‐
i) 7A/7B Proceedings:

The contents of the circular No.RRC/28(31)07/53677‐53777 dated 17.10.07 are
reiterated  for  strict  compliance.  Enquiries  under  Section  7A  are  often  seen  as
opportunities for indulging in malpractices and it is for the authorities specified in
the said circular to carry out supervisory checks in letter and spirit. Any laxity on
this  count  by  any  of  the  supervisory  officers  shall  not  be  countenanced  and
appropriate action shall be initiated. It is often seen that scrutiny of orders is done in
a routine manner without making serious efforts to pin‐point irregularities and take
necessary corrective action. At the other end of the spectrum, it is seen that some
officers  embark  on  an  avoidable  dissection  of  the  orders  passed,  at  times  even
imputing motives where none exist, reducing the entire exercise to a fault‐finding
mission.  This  should  not  be  persisted  with  and  the  scrutiny  exercise  shall  be
undertaken  with  objectivity  and  sincerity  so  that  the  twin  purposes  behind  the
same, that is, bringing about qualitative improvement and identifying irregularities
are served.
The assessing officer is a quasi judicial authority who has to pass a speaking
and  reasoned  order.  Most  of  the  time,  the  orders  passed  u/s  7A/7B/14B  are  not
speaking  and  therefore  are  quashed  whenever  challenged  before  a  Court  of  Law.
