Sub:- Special Drive on arresting defaults and liquidating arrear dues —-
Reg.

Sir,

Attention is invited to the various circulars containing revised instruction
for handling the cases initiated under section 7A, 7B, 7C and 14B of the Act, the
role of supervisory officials in initiation, disposal as well as quality checks of 7A
cases, distribution of compliance work amongst the officers, conduct of business
and fixing of targets in compliance area, Recovery targets and observation of
Recovery month etc..

However, an overall view of performance on compliance parameters of
field offices, it is observed that desired focused and sincere efforts are yet to be
taken. Although, there are existing guidelines and targets for all work areas,
with half of the financial year only remaining in hand, requirement for revisiting
and redefining targets and fixing accountability to achieve the target has been
strongly felt to meet the dead line. The Petitions Committee of Parliament
having taken stalk of the situation has also directed to devise suitable action
plan and propose steps to arrest defaults and to liquidate existing dues with
proper Action Plan.

Therefore following directions are reiterated in view of the observation of
Petitions Committee; to achieve the targets in compliance area with due
participation and responsibility of all concerned. All RPFCs and Zonal ACCs are
requested to meticulously follow the drill prescribed herewith and ensure
compliance under intimation to Head Office.

Initiation and disposal of 7A/14B cases:-

e Initiation of Timely action in all defaulting establishments is of
utmost importance and should be ensured by reviewing the
position on monthly basis by RPFC and zonal ACC.

e The target for reasonable disposal of cases per month, per assessing
officer should be strictly adhered.

e All 7A cases pending for more than one year should be disposed of by
31%December, 2010.

ACC, Zone to review the position of initiation and disposal of 7A cases on
monthly basis for all the offices under his jurisdiction while RPFC-I shall
also review the position at his level and issue necessary instruction to the
officer handling the compliance matter in his administrative capacity for
expeditious disposal of the case.

EO should be utilized for finalization of dues u/s 7A, inspection of
establishment not inspected since the date of coverage especially those
covered after 01-04-2001, recovery of dues, coverage of new
establishment, inspection of defaulting establishment, detecting defaults
etc. This is only elaborative and not exhaustive.

All field Officers should strictly follow the distribution of work related to 7A
cases as per Head Office guidelines. The Officers should not exceed to
their jurisdiction in any case without prior consent of head office. ACC,
Zone to confirm the position about conduct of 7A by the Authorized
Officers only in their field offices.

Realization of Current Demand :-

The target for realization on current demand will continue to remain as
100% for each Assessing Officer. However, it has been found that
Assessing Officers do not invoke timely recovery action for realization of
current dues which later on converts into arrear and NIR dues.

All Assessing Officers to ensure timely action, immediately on completion
of time prescribed in the 7A order and do not allow defaulter to go for
dilatory tactics to make the realization difficult.

Realization of Arrear Dues :-

All recovery action as prescribed u/s 8B to 8G of the Act has to be
ensured in all certificate cases. The Recovery Officer shall ensure all
recovery action to recover the dues by thoroughly scrutinizing the details.
All Offices should prepare the Dossier of each defaulting establishment
showing details of all RRCs issued, amount with period, date of
assessment, details of responsible person of the establishment, movable &
immovable asset of the establishment, legal status & details of stay if any
with terms and condition of stay etc. along with any other detail as
thought fit to recover the dues.

It is expected that all field offices are following the prescribed time
schedule of issue of Recovery Certificate which is by the first week of April
with duly incorporating all the details regarding nature of dues, period of
default, account wise details, details and address of the defaulting
establishment and its responsible officers. The Assessing Officer should
also provide all the support and share all available information in
compliance file with Recovery Officer .

The target for Arrear dues remains 80% for the Recovery Officers
including NIR dues.

The EOs should be exclusively utilized for the recovery of dues related to
their area.

It has been further decided that unlocking the NIR dues would be
the priority area of work of Recovery Officer for the remaining part
of the financial year.

Conversion of NIR into IR:-

There should be a special emphasis in recovering the locked up arrears by
converting NIR into IR by utilizing Recovery machinery in full strength.
The target in this regard is fixed as minimum 50% of the total NIR dues.

This has to be achieved by making extra efforts to get the stay vacated,
filing special petition for early hearing of pending cases, getting claims

Sub: Filing of Special Leave Petitions before the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
Sir,
Proposals for moving Special Leave Petitions in the Supreme Court of India
arising out of orders of various High Courts and NCDRC are received in the Head Office
as a routine course.
The procedure for filing SLPs has been laid down in 'The Supreme Court Rules,
1966'. The same can be accessed on the website of the Supieme Court of India. It is
desirable that the same are downloaded from the website and circulated among all
officers dealing with the subject for their benefit of knowledge of procedure to be
followed.
It is to be appreciated that the procedures going into a SLP have to be meticulously
observed right from the origin of the issue.
An earlier circular letter vide No LC/2(623)08/KR/36153 dated 12/9/08
enumerating the requisite documents which need to be sent while forwarding a proposal
for SLP in the first instant is to be reemphasize& The requirements laid down were in
keeping with the rules in this regard as aforementioned.
It is therefore advised that of while forwarding a proposal for SLP the same should
accompanied with a complete dossier containing.
(i)Copy of the Writ Petition filed before the Hon'ble High Court (Single
Bench/Division Bench) or NCDRC.

(P. Sudha
Additional C.P.F.C.
mpliance)
(ii) Copy of the Single Bench order of Hon'ble High Court.
(iii) Original certified copy of the Division Bench order of Hon'ble High Court or
the order of Hon'ble High Court against which SLP is proposed to be filed
and the original certified copy of NCDRC order, as the case may be.
(iv) Brief history of the case.
(v) English translated copies of all the documents if originally in Hindi or any
other language.
(vi) Draft application for condonation of delay wherever applicable.
(vii) Draft SLP duly enclosing legible copies of proposed annexures.
(viii) Copy of legal opinion of the advocate specifically mentioning the substantial
question of law of general importance to be decided by the Hon'ble Supreme
Court.
It may please be appreciated that the Regions where the cause of SLP arise are
supposed to be most conversant with the facts in the matter. So, it is necessary that the
SLP complete in all details should be got prepared there only in consultation with our
panel advocates in the respective High Courts so that delay in filing could be avoided.
These instructions are to be adhered to strictly.
Yours faithfully,

Sub: Introduction of SMS system in EPFO.

Sir,

It gives me great pleasure to announce launching of SMS _ based
communication platform of EPFO. It is a state of art communication platform
using which EPFO will be able to proactively communicate with all customers.
Implementation of this system will go a long way in complete automation of
establishing a central depository of data-base of Employers and Employees.

We are pleased to inform that a comprehensive solution based on the needs of
EPFO has been customised with the help of BSNL and IS Division. The solution shall offer
a centralised SMS, based communication platform which will be connected with all 120
field offices. The SMS service has been taken up for the employees, employers and EPFO
officials. The range of services to be provided are explained below in brief:-

SMS facility for the PF_Member

1. Automatic SMS Broadcast of Claim, Pension settlement and NEFT transfer.

2. Automatic SMS Broadcast to all EPF account holders at the end of the month
regarding their account balance.

3. SMS broadcast informing the missing information/document on receiving the Ciaiivis
from PF beneficiary.

4. PF Customers will themselves be able to get information of their PF balance
ensuring that information is passed on to the right person.

5. Anytime from anywhere the PF claimant may check up their claim status by sending
their “Claim ID”.

SMS facilities for the Employer:-

Registration/updation of mobile Number of the Establishemnt

Remittance status

Return status

Send SMS alert to companies informing short/excess payment, when the
Company files return.

SMS service for the EPFO staff shall also commence simultaneously by way of

Group SMS

Scheduled SMS

Flash SMS

SMS based Project monitoring

All the Officer Incharge are requested to take some extra effort to collect the mobile
numbers of all the employers and subscribers (employees) of the establishments
covered under their jurisdiction. The following may be done for collecting the mobile
numbers.

a) A separate column for providing mobile number be given in the daim form.
On pre-printed stationery, a rubber stamp for the same may be fixed while
distributing the claim form.

b) The mobile numbers of all the pensioners may be got collected by writing to
them to their addresses given in the file.

c) The establishment may be asked to provide its own mobile number under
the signature of authorised signatory.

d) The employer may also be encouraged to provide the mobile number of their
employees. This may be done by the employer in the following format.

Sub:- Suggestions for decoding of covered establishments/factories-reg.
Sir,

Your attention is invited to the minutes of the Review Meeting
taken by the CPFC on 24" and 25" May, 2010 at Head Office, New Delhi.
During the meeting, the various issues of compliance including allotment of
code number to contractor leading to inoperative accounts was also discussed
in detail. During the discussion, it was pointed out by some of the Additional
CPFCs that there are several covered establishment which are no longer in
existence and whose where abouts are not traceable. Maintaining accounts of
such establishments increases the workload of the office and is a non
productive work. In this regard, CPFC observed that the procedure of
decoding the establishments requires to be given a relook.

As per existing instruction and understanding, the covered
establishments can be decoded by holding proceedings u/s 7A or by the order
of a court. There are no administrative procedures and guidelines in vogue.
Therefore, as desired by CPFC, to revisit the issue and frame the suitable
procedural guidelines and policy for decoding of such establishment within the
legal provisions, your valued comments and suggestions are solicited which
may reach by 26" July, 2010 positively.

You are further requested to obtain and send the views of field
offices under your jurisdiction also.

Yours faithfully

(P. Sudhakar u

Sub: Application received in Form 13 (R) from the subscribers for Transfer of PF
accumulations — Quick disposal thereof - Regarding.

Sir,
The provisions of Section 17A of the EPF & MP Act 1952 and Para 57 of the EPF
Scheme 1952 enable an employee to transfer his PF accumulations consequent upon change in

his employment from one Region to another Region and in the establishmentswithin the same
Region.

Instances have come into the notice of Head Office where number of applications are
received in the field offices in Form 13 (R) for transfer cases under the above provisions but
could not be transferred by ane reason or another. The time for transfer takes lot of time from
one account to another and even after settlement of current account where the funds of earlier
account would have been credited on such transfer. As a result of this, such fund lies as
‘Inoperative Fund’ due to non availability of member’s account. This being one measure by
which number of inoperative accounts are increasing day by day.

Accordingly, it is advised that all the Inter/Intra Regional transfer cases received in
Form 13 (R) be dis ff on priority basis within the time frame as stipulated for settlement
of PF claims so as to minimize the grievances on non transfer of funds.

Yours faithfully,

(ABHAY K. SIN
Financial Advisor & Chief Account

ABOUT ZONAL TRAINING
INSTITUTE
(NORTH ZONE)

The Zonal Training Institute, North Zone,
Faridabad-now known as Dr, Syama Prasad Mookerjee
Institute of Social Security Administration (SPMISSA),
was set up in the year 1993 under the administrative
control of National Academy for Training & Research in
Social Security (NATRSS), New Delhi to meet the
challenges of Human Resource Development in
Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO),
Ministry of Labour & Employment, Govt. of India. This
Institute is primarily meant for imparting training to the
EPFO Staff in North Zone covering, Head Office
(Delhi), Delhi, Haryana, Himachal Pardesh, Punjab,
Uttar Pardesh & Uttaranchal.

Employee’s Provident Fund Organisation is the
world’s largest publicly managed Social Security
Organisation administring Provident Funds & Providing
Pension benefits to the persons employed in the Public
and Private Sector in India except State of Jammu &
Kashmir. It operates three Schemes viz Employees’
Provident Fund Scheme, 1952, Employees’ Pension
Scheme, 1995 (replacing Employees’ Family Pension
Scheme, 1971) and Employees’ Deposit-Linked
Insurance Scheme, 1976.

The Zonal Training Institute, North Zone, Faridabad
under direction and advice of the NATRSS has
undertaken the task of apprising, in stages, the members,
employees and employers, of the establishments
covered under the Employees’ Provident Fund Act about
the object and salient provisions of the PF Act & the
Schemes framed thereunder with a view to ensure
effective implementation of the Schemes for extending
benefits and social security to the working classes
through Seminars, Workshops at lowest possible cost.

The Zonal Training Institute North Zone
(SPMISSA) Faridabad is housed in its own complex
since 10th June ‘02 and is having sufficient expertise,
space and infrastructure for arranging one or more
training courses simultaneously for the Employers of
covered establishment / EPF Members or the members
of Board of Trustee of Exempted Establishments in the
above Regions. The institute has organised numerous
workshops and seminars every calender year since
2003-04, There has been unprecedented response to all
workshops and seminars organised for the benefit of
employers as well as employees of establishments
covered under EPF & MP Act, 1952.

Sub: Proper representation of our cases in the courts - reg.
Sir,
It has been felt that many a times our cases at different judicial fora are
not properly represented / defended. While there could be various reasons for
such instances, in large number of cases we loose the case just because our
advocate fail to bring to the notice of the courts the mandate of the EPF & MP
Act, 1952 and our contentions are not understood in right spirits of the
legislature.
In order to do away with this deficiency it is decided that all our counter
replies / submissions before the courts should start with a Preamble bearing on
the issue so that the courts may appreciate the subject matter in view of the
mandate of the Act.
A sample introductory para / preamble of counter reply is being enclosed
herewith for use in all our cases before the courts with suitable alterations
depending upon the situation.
You are requested to hold conference with all our advocates on panel and
impress upon them for the needful to be done. An action taken report in this
regard may please be sent.

The Employees' Provident Fund & Misc. Provisions Act, 1952 (EPF
& MP Act, 1952) is a legislation for providing social security to employees
working in any establishment engaging 20 or more persons on any day. It
provides for compulsory deduction of provident fund from employees and
a contribution from the employer which is deposited in the worker's
account in the EPF office.
Similarly, the Act also provides for providing insurance and
pensionary benefits to the employees.
The provident fund and other contributions have to be deposited by
the employer by the 15th of the next month in which the employee has
worked in the establishment and the dues become payable to him,
because the worker has already performed the employment upto last day
of the previous month.
The contributions have to be deposited by the
employer/establishment only after beneficiary worker has already worked
and thus earned this amount in terms of the contract of employment and
the provisions of the Act.
As such, any effort by the employer to deny employees the
legitimate dues which they have rightfully earned in terms of the
provisions of the Act, need to be looked upon with suspicion, whatever the
reason giyen by such employer/establishment.
In case of failure to deposit the legitimate dues of workers, the
EPFO under section 7A of the Act initiate recovery action for the purpose
of compelling the employer to deposit the legitimate dues of the worker.
Through a quasi-judicial process, the dues of the workers under section
7A of the Act is assessed and the employer/establishment is asked to
deposit the amount.
Subsequently, after deposit of the principal amount, action is
initiated to levy penalty and damages under section 7Q and Section 14 of
the Act to provide for the interest on the delayed payment by the employer
and also act as deterrence for them.
It is often seen that employer/establishment resort to filing the
petition in the Court once the recovery process has been started, which in
any case start after default of the legitimate dues have been committed by
such employer. The employers file such cases with a view to defeat the
object of the social security legislation, which provides for a lumpsum

Sub: Pending court cases and appointment of Advocates / Counsels -
ensuring speedy trials.

Sir,

It has been observed that there are a large number of court cases pending in
various regions where prima-facie, no action seems to have been taken either by
our Advocates/Regional/Sub-Regional Offices to get the matter disposed off
quickly. This was also discussed in the review meeting of the ACCs held on 24" &
25 May, 2010 at Head Office.

e As discussed, ACCs will henceforth review all the court cases every month
and ensure that cases are promptly attended to at our end, at the admission
stage itself, so that most of the frivolous petitions may be got dismissed at
the admission stage itself. The first such review shall be conducted by the
10™ of July and details of all the cases pending as on 31.03.10 before
different courts may be furnished to the Head Office in the format enclosed.

e When a case has been admitted, it should be the duty of advocate and the
Regional/Sub-Regional Office concerned to ensure that our replies are filed
without delay and expeditious decision obtained from the court by complying
with all legal formalities within the shortest time.

e Whenever any stay has been granted, it should be reviewed and steps taken
to ensure that the stay is vacated.

e In all such cases, our efforts should be to ensure that adjournments are
strongly opposed and that the tactics of delaying legal process by the
petitioners is not allowed and effectively argued before the courts.

e The performance of all the advocates empanellied for all the offices of the
Zones should be reviewed at the end of March & September every year and
where necessary the panel has to be redrawn. A format is being enclosed
herewith for review of performance of advocates and sending a report to HO.
The performa (I & II) for empanelment has been revised and is enclosed in
which the Regional Office should send their proposals through ACC (Zone)
for consideration.

e Regions which have not yet sent the panel for the new block year are

directed to forward their proposals in the revised formats without waiting for
reminder.

e In each Regional/Sub-Regional Office, there should not be more than few
advocates depending on the number of cases so that the advocates can
effectively attend to these cases.

e It is proposed to draw up a first panel of advocates based on their
performance so far and for this purpose a necessary format should be got
completed by RO/SRO and sent to us at the earliest. Please ensure that this
process is completed by 10" July, 2010.

e It is emphasized that the performance of the Regional/Sub-Regional Office
and officers connected with Legal Cell in these offices will be monitored
strictly and adverse view taken in case of laxity. ACCs should regularly
monitor these cases every month in a review meeting and legal issues
should also be discussed along with other issues of compliance etc. Cases
where important judgments have been obtained by EPFO should be
circulated to all offices by the concerned RO/SRO with copy to the
headquarter.

e Moreover, the primary responsibility of defending the case lies with the
officer whose order/statutory action has been challenged before the court.
Such officer should take all responsibility in deciding the line of argument,
preparation of counter replies, briefing the advocate, providing all the
material records and remaining present in the court, if required.

e It has been decided to call for the details of all the writ petitions/applications
pending before different courts in the format enclosed. Zonal ACCs may
ensure to forward it by10th July2010 positively.

Copy of this letter may also be sent to the concerned Regional/Sub-Regional Office
to comply with the above directions.

[This issues with the approval of CPFC]

Yours faithfully,

Encl.: 1. Proforma I & II
2. Proforma for review of performance of Advocate
3. Proforma for sending details of WP/EPFAT cases

explore the possibility of having a single return to be filed by the Employers

made to integrate the data being received from the establishments through

submitted their recommendations for the new format with their views that
such form may be introduced with an idea that it can be submitted in soft
form by the employers which will save EPFO from data entry work and also
remove data entry error related problems. An e-return tool is also being
developed for distribution amongst the employers to enable them to
generate the returns in soft as well as hard copy by data entry/upload at
their end.

• Sub: Cleaning of data and filling up of data gaps.
It has been observed by the Internal Audit during its audit of many offices that the
Residual and Negative Balances are on ever increase and the efforts of field offices in
cleaning the incorrect data appears to be abysmal. Instructions have already been
issued from time to time on actions required to be taken by field offices for removing the
Negative Balances and Residual Balances to ensure a clean and correct Form-24. In
order to initiate appropriate measures, the problems have been identified and defined in
the following paras with corrective actions required to be taken step-wise:'
A. Negative Balance
Negative Balances are the cases where there- is minus balance or the balance in the
Members Account instead of as positive balance. This can be due to various reasons:
1. The member was paid more amount by clerical mistakain calculation.
2. The amount pertaining to some other member is debited to negative balance
account by error.
3. Withdrawal made by advance is not accounted for while settlement of account is
made as per ledger and at the time of preparation of Form — 24 the same is
entered.
4. Difference in Form-3A received for broken period being more than the Form-3A
received at the end of the year. However; this amount would be very meager and
not likely to be more than one month contribution.
5. Settlement of account by adding transfer-in in ledger but not record the same in
Form-24.
In case of negative balances wherever the payment is actually in excess of what is due,
this can be rectified only by credit of equal amount to the account either by the recovery
from member or employer or the officials responsible for overpayment.. The available

2

machinery of OPRC must be used in its full form for rectifying these. Wherever the
negative balance is due to error in accounting the same can be rectified by counter
entries with proper noting and proof by way of documents like Annexure K etc, under the
approval of at least APFC level Officer. The Negative Balances occurring mainly due to
non cash transfer, that is transfer within the office without any cheque payment etc, also
need to be treated as actual overpayment due to negligence.

Correcting Negative Balances:
Likely Reasons for Negative Balances:
1. Paid more amount by clerical mistake in calculation.
2. The amount pertaining to some other member is debited to negative balance
account by error.
3. Withdrawal made by advance is not accounted for while settlement of account is
made as per ledger and at the time of preparation of Form – 24 the same is
entered.
4. Difference in Form-3A received for broken period being more than the Form-3A
received at the end of the year. However, this amount would be very meager and
not likely to be more than one month contribution.
5. Settlement of account by adding transfer-in in ledger but not record the same in
Form-24.
6. SRF Amounts

In all the above cases, the note sheet approved by the APFC and other documents
taken as proof for rectification form permanent records and must be retained alongwith
the Form 24 concerned. These documents are subject audit by Internal and External
Audit. Detailed stepwise procedure for rectification of Residual Balances is given in
Annexure-I.

B. Residual Balance

The Residual Balances are those balances left out in the member’s account after final
settlement under Para 69 of the Scheme. This may occur due to many reasons:

a. Some credit coming subsequent to member leaving the service and withdrawing
the money, particularly, by way of arrears paid by establishment.
b. This can also be due to difference in Form-3A furnished during withdrawal of
balances and received during year end where the year end Form 3A shows higher
balance than the earlier one.
c. Some transfer-in amount getting credited subsequently to members leaving and
final settlement.
d. A portion of amount retained by office due to improper compliance or minus
balances in DCBR. Office, generally as a practice, retains proportionate amount
for minus balance in DCBR during final settlement.
e. Non debit of any withdrawal by way of advances during the membership period
and taken in ledger while settling the Form-19 but not entered in Form-24. It is

whereby e-payment module for payment to EPF beneficieries was launched in 91 Unix driven legacy offices. The
revised version of e-payment module for legacy offices has been prepared and uploaded on EPFO website with
following additional features:-

a) Provision to feed subscribers Mobile Number in database.
b) Addition of subscribers Bank Account Number in summary sheet as per bank’s requirement.
c) Transaction details in subscriber's account to reflect “NEFT EPFO” for clarity on source of payment.

The revised software patch is also accompanied with e-payment reconciliation tool, to be run on stand alone
computer system. This tool will enable generation of reconciliation reports in MS-Excel for minimizing manual
reconciliation. The reconciliation exercise has to be carried summary sheet date wise and chronological sequence
of activities for reconciliation are as below:-

e VB Tool named NEFT Compare Utility to be loaded in system in NEFT_RECO folder.

e All EPFO text files generated by system (NEFT and CBS) to be placed in EPFO_TXT folder for summery
sheet date.

e All NEFT upload (Bulk NEFT transaction) report given by bank irrespective of summary sheet date to be
kept in R1_NEFT_TXT_REP folder cumulatively.

e All CBS (trickle feed transaction) reports given by bank irrespective of summary sheet date to be kept in
R1_SBI_TXT_REP folder cumulatively.

e Latest return MIS for NEFT (downloaded HTML file) to be kept in R2_NEFT_HTML_REP folder.
e = Click reconcile button on NEFT compare utility.

e MS-Excel summary sheet will be generated providing status receipt number wise.

e = =Manual reconciliation of all pending and rejected cases with Cash Book.

e Generation of pending and rejected cases for follow up with Link Branch and claiming amount lying with
Bank Suspense Account and Parking Account.

Sub: Instructions for following the Government directives on Air Travel
on official account for both Domestic and International.
Sir,
Various references have been received from various quarters seeking
clarification on the following of the instructions of the Government of India on
undertaking of Air Travel on official duties:
02.
In this connection it is stated that the instructions of the
Government of India as already communicated vide Office Memorandum No
F.19024/1/2009-E-IV, dated 13-07-2009 of Department of .Expenditure,
Ministry of Finance, Government of India are very clear. AccOrding to these
instructions (i) All cases of Air Travel, both Domestic and International, where
the Government of India bears the cost of Air passage, the Offlcials concerned
may travel only by Air India and (ii) for travel to stations not connected by Air
India, the officials may travel by Air India to the hub/point closest to their
eventual destination, beyond which they may utilize the services of another
airline which should also preferably be an alliance partner of Air India.
When the Air India Flight is available in a particular sector, the travel by private
air line is not permissible simply on the ground that the timings are not suitable
and the flights are being operated on particular days only.
03.In view of the above, the travels by Private Airlines is irregular, and as such
the payments made if any, for whatsoever exigencies for the travels in Private
Airlines after the issuance of the above instructions of 13-07-2009 may be
recovered forthwith.
04. In view of the clear instructions of the Government as stated at Para 02
above, any proposal for Relaxation in this regard which is to be referred to
the Ministry of Civil Aviation will not be considered and therefore the ,above
instructions may be complied with strictly.
(This issues with the approval of FA & CAO)

Sub: Settlement of claims out of In-operative Accounts- regarding

It is observed that a large amount is lying in in-operative account. This amount

pertains to members/their family members and the same has to be paid back to them.
Considering the mandate of EPFO, it has been decided that:

ils

Special Drive may be launched by all the regions to settle these accounts to the
rightful claimants or to transfer the amount to their present account. Initially the inoperative accounts having balance of more than Rs.5, 000/- may be targeted for
this exercise.

Special drive may be launched by giving press release through newspapers and
Akashvaani_spots informing that EPFO has been launching a drive in order to
facilitate withdrawals of PF deposits of those subscribers who have left their amount
for over 3 years which have since been lying non-operative.

Enforcement Officers may be deputed to the establishments having more number
of such accounts to give list of such accounts to the employers and to get the
addresses of such members as per employers’ records. Individual members may be
addressed on the given addresses so obtained.

A list of such accounts may be given to recognized unions of establishments and
their help may be sought to approach the rightful claimant.

Form 2, in respect of such members may be searched out and the members may
be contacted at the address available therein.

It may be checked through EO and employers that existing contributing members

are not having multiple accounts in the in-operative accounts. Multiple accounts be
closed or transferred.

. The claims should be settled duly observing all formalities and checks prescribed in

Manual of Accounting Procedure and instructions issued by Headquarters in this
regard to ensure that correct payment is affected to the genuine claimants.

While reporting the amounts in the in-operative accounts in the returns or in annual
accounts of the regions, only those accounts which strictly fulfill the conditions
prescribed in Para 72(6) of EPF Scheme, 1952 should be reported. The OIC

concerned should check and certify the figures of in-operative accounts before
sending to Headquarters.

Para 72(6) of the EPF Scheme 1952 has the provision that (i) supplementary
contributions received from the employer on account of any reason in respect of the
member whose claim has been settled but could not be remitted for want of address
or (ii) accumulation in respect of any member who has either ceased to be employed
or died but no claim has been preferred within a period of three years from the date it
becomes payable or any amount remitted fo a person is received back undelivered
and is not claimed again within 3 years from the date it becomes payable, shall be
transferred to In-operative Accounf. In case of a claim for the payment of fhe
balance, the amount shall be paid by debiting the In-operative Account.

9. All the field offices should ensure that in-operative accounts kept in registers before
introduction of CAPS are brought into regular Form 24 with due interest without any
omission. No such accounts should remain outside the F/24 hereafter.

The above steps shall be initiated without any delay and a Compliance Report in
this regard shall be sent to the Headquarters. Weekly progress in the matter should be
reported by ACCs every Monday in the enclosed pro-forma. A consolidated report
including all ROs/SRO’s may be furnished by 30.06.2010. The progress achieved should
be reported in the prescribed monthly return FB-7 also. FA & CAO would monitor the

progress periodically.

Sub: Implementation of e-payment Modalities

This has reference to OM No.Bkg.1(25)/NEFT/Electronic Data Transfer/2087 dated
28/29.04.2010 whereby e-payment modalities for releasing payment to beneficiaries

was introduced for Unix based legacy offices.

The target date for completion of e-payment modalities was fixed as 10.05.2010

and reports suomitted have been reviewed.

It is noted with deep concern that as on 11.05.2010 only 23 offices have furnished
returned MIS received from SBI. The upload report has been submitted by 31 offices
who failed to obtain returned MIS from SBI. Collectively, implementation report has
been received from 54 offices only indicating a shortfall of 40% in implementation of

e-payment modalities.

ACC(HR & RJ) and ACC(GJ & MP) have put in sincere efforts and have
achieved appreciable performance. However ACC(AP & OR}, ACC(DL & UT),
ACC(KN & GOA), ACC(MH & CHH), ACC(TN & KR) and ACC(WB & NER) have not been

able to achieve 100% target.

Detailed guidelines for implementation of e-payment module have already

been circulated. The process flow at SBI for NEFT implementation has also been mailed

to all offices. Despite this, 37 offices have failed to implement the e-payment module

which is not acceptable.
It is reiterated that implementation of e-payment modalities is a high priority area

and all legacy offices should complete the implementation exercise within two days.

Any problem faced in implementation process to be resolved at Head Office level

Sub: Convening of Review Meeting of Regional Provident Fund Commissioners.
Sir,

I am directed to state that the Central Provident Fund Commissioner has directed
to organize the review meeting of Regional Provident Fund Commissioners in the 40
Regions in political states as per the schedule of date as per Annexure-I enclosed. The
venue for the review meeting for all the zones would be at NATRSS, New Delhi.

2. Review structure: As in the past the performance review will be in two parts.
In the first part Addl. CPFC, of the zone shall review the performance of the RPFCs Incharge and the SROs under his jurisdiction on the basis of the performance in the core
work areas i.e., coverage, recovery of arrears, annual accounts and settlement of claims
achieved during the 2009-2010. The targets achieved after midterm review done in
October 2009 would also be highlighted in their review. The reasons for not achieving the
targets would also be brought out clearly indentifying the impediments. In the second
part, the CPFCs review meeting would be at headquarters in which the review conducted
by the Addl. CPFCs would be discussed. The focus area would be improvement in service
delivery area. This would indude settlement of claims within 30 days, clearance of
backlog of accounts statements to subscribers and drastic improvements in grievance
redressal of subscribers and employers. The targets for the current financial year 2010-11
and strategy for achieving the targets would be discussed.

3. Proforma for review meeting: The performance statistics for review meeting
will be provided by the Addl. CPFCs consolidated for the Regions under their jurisdiction.
The proforma in excel sheet format (.xis files) has been mailed separately to all Addl.
CPFCs and RPFCs in-charge to the official e-mail IDs. It may be ensured that the data is
fed in excel sheet proforma only and consolidated for each Region and then consolidated
for the zone.

4. Review by Addl. CPFC level: The Addl. CPFCs of the zone would consolidate the
performance data Region wise and send it back duly filled to Headquarters by 14"
May 2010 by email at sanjay.bisht@epfindia.gov.in or rc.conf@epfindia.gov.in.

discussion in the review meeting to be taken by the CPFC. The Addl. CPFCs will conduct

focus on service area. In this regard the observations of the CPFC contained in DO letter
No. MIS.3 (1)/RFD/MOLE/2009-10 dated 3™ May 2010 may kindly be referred. The Addl.
CPFCs would complete their review of the Regions and offices under their
jurisdiction by 14 May 2010 positively.

taken by the CPFC with his team of Divisional Heads in which all the zonal Addl. CPFCs and
RPFCs In-charge as indicated in the Annexure would also be present. The Addl. CPFC, of
the Zone will apprise the CPFC of the performance review taken by him highlighting the
areas where shortfall had been recorded and the reasons for such shortfall under each
work area. Based on the inputs the Addl. CPFC and the RPFC in-Charge, would make a
presentation to set the business goals under each core areas with targets and the time
lines for achieving the targets spelt out for the four quarters for the current financial year
in respect of the Region under his jurisdiction.

6. The specific discussion points that will be raised by the divisional heads at
Headquarters and programme structure would be sent separately.

Dear Sir,
As, you may be aware the Modernization Project developed in collaboration with NIC has been
implemented in 28 offices of the organization. The rollout of the project in the remaining 'offices of the
organization will follow as a natural denouement of the process of computerization.
As the project has to be implemented in all the offices, it is felt that drawing upon the experience gathered
from the implementation in the 28 offices, a set of advanced preparatory actions should be taken up by
every office with a view to.ease the process of implementation. Accordingly, the measures proposed below
may be initiated by each office.
I. GENERAL DATA CLEANING AND MEMBER ACCOUNTS UPDATING ACTIVITIES
(A) Updating Member Accounts: Annual accounts of members should be updated and aecounts slips
be issued in accordance with . the provisions contained in the Accounting Manual. Contributions,
transfers in/out, withdrawals and final settlements must be accounted for properly. Errors, if any,
should be rectified through appendix "E" entries as per the procedure prescribed in this regard. If
unauthenticated and unapproved data is migrated to the new system, the same will result in
overpayments and the necessary safeguards must be applied to avoid such lapses. The officers-incharge of respective offices are, therefore, advised to ensure that account slips are issued after
proper 'reconciliation and authentication and as per the procedure laid down in the Accounting
Manual. Annual accounts for the current year and also for the period prior to current year must•
Completed and annual accounts slips be issued to •the maximum extent possible.
(B) Data Cleaning: It has been observed that multiple PF account numbers have been allotted in
respect of certain members, due to a variety of reasons, in the legacy system which has resulted in
multiple PF balancei in respect of such members with 'Empm.dbf' containing many
duplicate/triplicate records. In the Data Migration strategy, it has been decided that opening
balance data available in respect of each member has to be verified with respect to the approved
Form-24 available in the AcCount groups'and if necessary the same, be corrected after following the

prescribed procedure. Further, while doing 310, following steps need be taken by the EDP

Before doing 310 activities for an establishment, execute 650/610/615 modules so that
deleted records will get packed.

After 310 activities, please ensure that no duplicate record is formed by checking through
501 module.

In order to migrate maximum records to the new system, checklist level, 3A receipt level,
F24/F23 level are to be brought to 310 level i.e. all pending F24/F23,checklists are to be
processed and 310 activity has to be done for all pending cases.

In respect of live and complying establishments, the annual accounts are required to be
updated only with contribution. However in case of permanently closed establishments, the
annual accounts can be updated without contribution i.e. by crediting interest only.

(C) Cash Book: It has also been decided that reconciled CRAS data would get migrated into the new
system. In order to ensure that proper cash book records are migrated to the new systems, the
Cash books in respect of A/c -01, 02, 10, 21, & 22 must be reconciled every month and closed up
to the month preceding the date of migration. The Officer-in charge of respective offices must
ensure that the Cash Books for all accounts are reconciled on regular basis by collecting Challans
and bank statements from SBI on weekly basis so as to avoid any pendency at the time of
migration.
(D) Pension: In order to ensure timely payment of monthly pension to the pensioners and to resolve
pension disbursement reconciliation issues, it has been decided to use Core Banking facilities of
banks which have been designated for disbursement of pension payments. For this purpose old S.B
A/c Numbers of Pensioners need to be replaced with new Core Banking S.B. A/c Number. This
activity need to be monitored personally by the officer-in-charge so as to ensure 100% updation of
data of Pensioners with regard to the Core Banking Saving Bank A/c Number. Matter may be
immediately taken up with the banks which have been designated for disbursement of pension for
getting the needful done. Apart from the above certain essential data which at present is in the
manual form also need to be captured in the electronic form so that the same can be migrated to
the new system. To facilitate capturing of such data and also for cleaning of the soft data, a
software namely Data Migration Capturing & Cleaning Software (DMCC) has been developed and
has been uploaded on EPFO website.

(A) Modular Furniture: The instructions issued by the Physical Facilities Division of Headquarters on
modular furniture for offices may be referred which contains, inter alia, the electrical and IT cabling
recommendations. As per present instructions, modular furniture may be installed in all office
premises that are owned by the organization. Actions necessary for completing this task may be
taken, if not already completed.
(B) Office Air-Conditioning: The instructions issued by the Physical Facilities Division of Headquarters
may be referred to and necessary action may be initiated.
(C) Generators: Instructions of Public Facilities Division may be referred to and the actions should be
initiated for installing generator of appropriate capacity taking into account the electrical load of
the premises.

Implementation of EPFiGMS-grievance management system of EPFO

EPFIGMS is an internet based grievance management system that has
been developed by CSD in collaboration with the NIC, customized to the
needs of the organisation. The EPFIGMS has been developed with a view to
provide a single window platform that is able to record, acknowledge and
track/monitor grievances till its final redressal.

The system would not only afford convenience to subscribers to
register their grievances /queries without any spatial or temporal restrictions
but should also prove to be of immense value to field offices in managing
grievances. Subscribers can access the system from anywhere and all paper
grievances can also be registered in the system.

It is loaded with several advanced features, most important being that
movement of registered grievance guided by database which would track the
registered grievance to any of the offices to which it might be related. Once
a grievance is registered, system would generate a unique registration
number and would auto generate acknowledgement letter directly to the
subscribers e-mail (if provided).

EPFiIGMS has a well defined escalation plan and allows thirty days time
to each office to redress the grievance. If any grievance remains unattended
up to thirty days, it would escalate to the next higher authority. In such
instances, the subordinate office would become answerable to the higher
authority to which grievances are escalated.

System also allows handling of grievances involving two or more
offices e.g. transfer or pension cases, where one office can provide only
partial redressal and remaining needs to be done by other office.

For effective implementation of EPFIGMS and monitoring of grievances
“Nodal Grievance officers” are designated as follows:

e ACC(Zone)- Nodal Grievance officer for entire Zone
e RPFC-I (In charge of —Region)- Nodal Grievance officer for entire Region
e Officer-In -charge SRO- Nodal Grievance officer for entire SRO.

Further, aS matter of policy, maximum time admissible to a field office
for redressal/reply of grievance is 30 days from the receipt of the grievance.
The ownership of the grievance would lie with the office which has generated
the grievance.

Each paper grievance received locally in the field offices have to be
mandatorily registered in the EPFIGMS. It may be ensured that system is not
bypassed in handling local grievances. Hence, necessary logistic support in
this regard may be provided in each office; also facilitation center/PRO of
each field office must be equipped with this system to register grievances of
visiting subscribers.

For Successful implementation of EPFiIGMS, It is important that its
Operation is performed under the supervision of Officer- in Charge/Nodal
Grievances Officers as designated above. A detailed standard operating
procedure is enclosed for information and guidelines.

An action taken report must be furnished within one week of receipt of

this instruction.

Implementation of National Ele.ctronic Fund Transfer(NEFT) for
payment th'EPF Beneficiaries.
The existing arrangement for payment to EPFO beneficiaries is paper based wherein payments are
released through individual account payee cheques or money orders. It is primarily a manual system involving
considerable time lag between authorization of claim and actual receipt of payment. This delay mainly occurs
on account of:-
i) Lag of many days between authorization of claim and printing of cheques.
ii) Time taken for signing of cheques due to large volumes.
iii) Long time taken for physical handing over of 'cheques and forwarding letter to Speed POst Center.
iv) Very tong time taken by Speed Post Centers.
v) Time taken in clearing of cheques.
This delays leads to generation of huge number of grievances which is a dear indicator of low level of
customer satisfaction. To overcome these in=efficiencies and to curtail the time lag between authorization of
claim and actual receipt of payment, modifications have been carried out in Unix based legacy system to avail
the electronic route of payment.
Ninety Five banks with over' 67,000 bianches are now connected to National Electronic Fund
Transfer(NEFT) network. Payment to these NEFT networked branches are effected six times a day through a
system driven by Reserve Bank of India. FAQ on NEFTisencloSed for ready reference and detailed procedural
guidelines may be accessed at http://rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/content/ridfs/65253.pdf. Payments to State
Bank of India (SBI) branches are also being effected through electronic route on Core Banking Solution(CBS)
platform. Day by day a large number of bank brandies are getting connected to NEFT network and only
Cooperative and Rural Banks are now out of the NEFT Grid. Gradually these banks will also be brought on the
network but till such time payments to these banks can be effected through cheque only. •
It gives us pleasure to launch e -payment in EPFO which will enable us to get the benefits credited to
members accounts within 1-2 days of claim authorization, leading to substantial reduction in grievances and
higher customer satisfaction.
The required software patch for implementation of e-payment has been prepared and uploaded on
EPFO website with necessary loading instructions and operation manual. You are requested to thoroughly
study these instructions and implement same in letter and spirit. This software patch will enable e-payment in
legacy system and a separate software patch enabling e-payment in Linux based new software will be released
shortly. Ninety One offices, operating on legacy software will thus have three modes of payment:
1. e-payment (CBS and NEFT).
2. Cheques for Non-Networked bank branches.
3. Money Orders for payments upto Rs.2000/- whenever desired by beneficiaries.
118

E-payment modalities will take up CBS or NEFT route based on the member's bank branch. All SBI
payments will be effected through CBS and payments to networked branches will be made through NEFT. The
software has been tested at RO, Gurgaon successfully. The e-payment through NEFT and CBS will now be
default option for disbursement and other two options may be oh-board for sometime as "fall-back" option; to
be used only if payment cannot be made electronically. The service charges for this service has been specified
by RBI as under:
a) Inward transactions at distribution bank branches for credit to beneficiaries accounts : Free
b) Outward transactions at origination bank branches (Charges for the remittances):-
For transactions upto Rs.1 lakh
: Charges not exceeding Rs.5
For transactions of Rs.1 lakh and above
: Charges not exceeding Rs.25

Sub: Forwarding of details in respect of International Workers deployed in
India — Regarding.

Sir,

Instructions have been issued from time to time regarding compliance
in respect of International Workers employed in covered establishments.
Special provisions relating to International Workers have been notified vide
gazette notification 01.10.2008, suitably amending the EPF Scheme, 1952
and Employees’ Pension Scheme, 1995. As on date, bilateral agreements
relating to Social Security have been implemented in respect of two
countries namely, Belgium (w.e.f. 01.09.2009) and Germany (w.e.f.
01.10.2009). Negotiations are in progress with other countries.

It is expected that the employers of covered establishments are
complying with the statutory provisions pertaining to International Workers
and depositing contributions on full salary of the International Workers.
Subsequent to the implementation of the Agreements with Belgium and
Germany, the employees from these two countries may have sought
exemption from contributing to the Indian Social Security System on the
basis of certificate of coverage/detachment certificate issued by the
respective competent body/agency. This certificate of coverage issued to an
International Worker confers on him the status of excluded employee,
whereby he continues to contribute to the Social Security System of his
country, and is exempted from contributing to the Indian Social Security
System.

You are, therefore, requested to instruct your Enforcement Officers
that while inspecting the records of an establishment to verify the
compliance status, they may also obtain the details of such excluded
employees possessing valid certificates of coverage in original. The details
in respect of such excluded employees may also be forwarded to Head
Office for information in the following format as and when any such
excluded employee is reported.

Sub: Strengthening and streamlining of Public Grievance Handling SystemArrangements for kiosks and Drop Boxes.
Sir,
Your attention is drawn to this office circular dated 20/21.07.2009, wherein
instructions were issued in the above matter. The matter has been reviewed and it is observed
that no acknowledgement for claim forms and returns dropped in the boxes are being issued,
which results into following difficulties:-
In the absence of acknowledgement the subscribers are finding it difficult to
follow up their claims. Instances of missing of claim forms dropped in the boxes
have also been noticed.
Settlement of claims has also been delayed, as it takes time to deliver the claims in

NEW FUND MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Under the NFMS, following procedure have been laid down:
In respect of those bank accounts wherein NFMS has been implemented, the nature of
Trustees' bank accounts would be Current A/c instead of Savings A/c.
All the cheques issued by the field offices would be honored by the respective link
branches irrespective to the balance available in the bank A/c;
At the end of the working day, whatever would be the closing balance in the accounts of
field offices, whether Debit or Credit, would be on-line transferred using auto sweep by all
the link branches to the Central Investment Accounts of the Trustees' maintained with SBIMain Branch Mumbai, leaving NIL balance in the accounts at Link Branch. All the transfers
(Debit / Credit) made by the field offices would be effected in the respective Central
Investment Accounts on the same day;
In case, there is surplus (Credit Balance) as the net balance in any Central Investment
Account then the same would be transferred to Security Services Branch of SBI at Mumbai
for investment on the same day;
In case, there is deficit (Debit Balance) as the net balance in any Central Investment
Account then the same will be taken care of out the consolidated overdraft limit extended
by the SBI-Main Branch, Mumbai to EPFO;
Any overdraft limit availed by EPFO on a particular day, would be squared off against the
surplus / inflows taken place on the immediate next day. Till this overdraft is squared off,
interest -would be charged by SBI on outstanding amount at a mutually agreed / specified
rate.
The overdraft limit may be increased / decreased at point of time with the mutual consent
of both the parties, considering the requirements of EPFO.
Although, there is a provision for auto transfer of daily closing balance from link branch to
SBI-Mumbai Main Branch, it would be the responsibility of the concerned link branch to
transfer the daily closing balance {Debit / Credit} to SBI-Mumbai Main Branch.
If Link Branch does not transfer any credit balance available on the same day, a penal
interest of 4% over and above the prevailing SBI Saving Bank Interest rate would be
payable on such amount retained by the SBI till it is transferred to Central Investment
Accounts. However, In case the link branch does not transfer any Debit balance there will
not be any charge on EPFO as the transfer of balance is the sole responsibility of SBI Link
Branches.
There will not be any additional charges on the transfer of daily closing balances by the link
branches to SBI-Mumbai Main Branch or vice versa.
The link branches shall provide the Regional Offices, Sub-Regional offices, the particulars
of balance available in the accounts maintained by them on daily basis and that the link
branches shall provide the facility of Remote log in / Internet Banking (wherever available)
to the respective field offices without any additional charges.
Settlement with regard to payment of service charges and claim of interest for delayed
credit, clearance of missing credits, un-reconciled amount or amount in transit pertaining to
past period shall be in accordance with the mechanism agreed in February 1998, the
relevant extracts of the same are as per Annexure- II.

Dear Sir,

It gives me immense pleasure in informing you that the Training Calendar of
the Academy for the year 2010-11 has been approved by the CPFC and the same
has been uploaded on the EPFO website. A copy is enclosed for your ready
reference.

The review of feedback from the training courses conducted last year and
inputs received through informal consultations with a cross section of officers
from corporate and field offices were factored in while designing the training
calendar. Altogether forty five training courses have been planned this year.

The overall objective of the planned training courses is to build the
functional competencies of the officers and enhance their managerial
effectiveness. Accordingly training courses in each of the functional areas of the
organization have been included in the plan. Similarly for enhancing managerial
Capacities, training courses have been designed in General Management,
Enhancing Managerial Effectiveness & Strategic Management targeted to Junior,
Middle and Senior management level officers respectively. We have also included
Workshops for employers of exempted and other establishments to discuss their
issues and disseminate latest updates from the organization.

As we are all aware the effectiveness and efficiency of training courses
depends to a large extent in having the right participants and that too in right
number. The low participation rate in various training courses in the Academy is
eroding their efficiency. Besides, not getting the right participants, especially in
the training courses in the functional areas is another challenge, the Academy is
grappling with. It is an established principle of adult learning that participants not
dealing with a particular subject will not be enthusiastic for learning in that area.
In order to stem these issues, the Academy seeks your active involvement and

training courses of the Academy will be nominated by the Regional Commissioner

The Central Board of Trustees, Employees' Provident Fund in its 188th Meeting
held on 05.12.2009 has approved the Revised Estimates for the year 2009-10 and

respect of your Region including SROs, as enclosed herewith. Please note that the
booking of Income & Expenditure should be classified clearly in Cash Book for
Account No. 2 and Classified Summary be sent to the Head Office on due date.
Instructions issued on financial discipline on earlier occasions should be followed
strictly.

relevant budget head only. The monthly expenditure in each head should be
incurred proportionately to the total budget allotment for the year 2010-11. As per
the proVisions of Chapter 5. of General Financial Rules, before sanctioning
expenditure, the Competent Authority should ensure that adequate budget provision
exists in the particular item. Incurring expenditure beyond the budget allotment is
contrary to the Financial Rules and should not be allowed in any case. In any
particular month, if the expenditure is likely.to be exceeded the budgetary. limit under
any particular head, then the same should have prior approval of FA&CAO. Any
amount spent over and above the allotment without prior approval as provided in
Para 58 of the EPF Scheme, 1952 will be treated as Incorrectly withdrawn, and will be
viewed very seriously. In case at any violation` In this regard, officers concerned for
such expenditure would be held responsible and accountable and It will render them
liable for action.

Subject: Finalization of Training Calendar for the year 2010-2011.
Sir,

Further to the consultations with you in the meeting held on 15 March
2010 at the Academy on the subject mentioned above, following principles and
guidelines are enunciated for finalization of the training calendar.

2s Training Calendar should include training programmes in five broad areas:
(i) Induction Training
(ii) Refresher Functional Skill Development Programme
(iii) Personality Development Programme
(iv) | Supervisory/Managerial Development Programme
(v) |Workshop for Employers/Employees

(i) Induction Training:

Induction training builds the foundation of functional competence of the
new entrants to the organization. Accordingly, each newly recruited staff
needs to be provided with induction training. ZTIs are advised to endeavor
to cover each staff with induction training within 1* year of his/her joining.

(ii) Refresher Functional Skill Development Programme:

Once provided with the induction training, it is expected that staff
members further develops his knowledge and skills in functional areas
through on the job learning and development.

However after some time, they need to refresh and update themselves with
the new developments in their respective functional areas. Accordingly
refresher training courses in following functional area should be organized:

e Accounts

e Compliance

e Pension

e Administration

87, xp

These programmes should focus on problems solving and discussion on
recent developments. These programmes should also incorporate module
on personality development and EPF Application software.

(iii) Personality Development Programmes: The personality of the
workforce impinges upon their performance and the functional efficiency of
the organization. National Training Policy has emphasized the significance of
training pertaining to the attitudinal development. Accordingly ZTIs should
design courses that will help develop certain positive trends in personality of
the staff members. At least one Personality Development Programme
should be administered once every two years to each staff.

(iv) Supervisory/Management Development Programme: The
managerial efficiency and style of the supervisory staff affects the
performance of personnel and productivity of their offices. Accordingly
efforts should be made to provide one such programme to each HC/AAO/EO
once in every two years.

(v) Workshop for Employers/Employees: The number and content of
these workshops may be decided based on the local needs and resources.

3. As discussed during the meeting held in the academy, proportion of training
programmes/days should be reasonably divided amongst functional and
behavioral/management development programmes. The broad contents of 20
training programmes in each of the areas mentioned above are enclosed.
However, minor adjustment and adaptation may be made keeping in view the
local needs and requirement.

4. As already agreed in the meeting held at NATRSS, in a five day training
course on functional area and Induction Training programme, two sessions on EPF
Application Software should be incorporated.

on Review of the training activities of the last year revealed that at an average
each ZTI had logged more than 250 training days and efforts should be made to
enhance it to 300 days this year.

6. It is requested that the Training Calendar may be finalized keeping in view
the guidelines as suggested above and forwarded to the Academy. The Training
Programmes as contained in your proposed calendar for April 2010 was already
approved vide this office letter No. 13(20)/2007/NATRSS/All ZTIs/5053-57 dated
4-03-2010.

Yours faithfully,
